| S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE | 2026-05-06 | Fix the rate-lookup endpoint at `api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php` — query by `equipment_templates.category` instead of `equipment_templates.name`. Bug surfaced as a bonus finding during S-MILEAGE-RATE-ZERO-FIX (commit bc4db87) and immediately spawned as carry-forward. **This is the upstream root cause of the entire zero-rate bug class** — fixing it stops new $0-rate leases from being created at the source by closing the silent fall-through that landed every Priority 1 + Priority 2 lookup on Priority 3 (template defaults). 2 commits + this docs entry. **Pre-work scan (Explore agent + direct grep across api/, app/, lib/, scripts/, tests/, cron/, db_migrations/, database/):** all 18 customer_equipment_rates rows + 18 rate_card_items rows + 11 customer_rate_history rows are category-form (`dry_van`, `chassis`, `reefer`, `flatbed`, `container`, `step_deck`, `lowboy`, `tanker`, `dump`); zero rows in template-name form. demo_seed.php + seed_dataset.php WRITE category-form. UI dropdowns at customers/show.php:980 + rates/create.php:173 + rates/show.php:238 WRITE template-name form via `$t['name']` — but UI write activity has been zero on live data (all rows came from seeds). Reports (api/v1/reports/{revenue,fleet}.php, compliance/index.php) read `equipment_templates.category` directly — never touch the rate tables for type matching. lookup_rates.php is the ONLY rate-matching reader; everything else is form-write or display-read. **Decision: Option A** (change lookup line 82 from `$template['name']` to `$template['category']`). Reasoning: (1) `equipment_templates.category` is an ENUM with finite values; `equipment_templates.name` is mutable VARCHAR(100). (2) Multiple templates can share a category — template 1 "53ft Dry Van" + template 6 "Seed: 53ft Dry Van Wabash" both = `dry_van` — per-category rate semantics are correct, per-template-name would fragment them. (3) Live data is already 100% category-form so zero data migration needed. (4) Option B (migrate data + seeds to template names) would have moved the schema in the wrong direction (away from the ENUM). **Commit 1 — fix ([7a45534](api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php)):** single-line semantic change (`$equipmentType = $template['category']`) plus 17-line docblock rewrite at lines 79-95 explaining the canonical convention, the historical bug, and the carry-forward UX issue (UI dropdowns still write template names). **Commit 2 — smoke ([7941148](tests/_smoke_lookup_rates.php)):** new end-to-end test covering all 4 priority paths via parent/child fork pattern (borrowed from tests/_smoke_payoff_api.php since the endpoint exits via json_response). T1+T2 customer hits on known cust/tmpl pairs (cust=1+tmpl=1 → $0.18/km dry_van, cust=4+tmpl=5 → $0.13/km chassis); T3 rate_card hit using customer 9 SMOKE-S4 test co (zero cer rows) + tmpl=1; T4 + T5 use two temporary `equipment_templates` with category='other' inserted by the parent (one with non-null defaults for Priority 3, one with NULL defaults for Priority 4); both deleted in finally regardless of outcome (test-pollution discipline — confirmed zero `__SMOKE_LOOKUP_RATES%` rows remain post-run). Plus a CONTROL assertion that the pre-fix query shape (template names) returns 0 rows on live data while the post-fix shape (categories) returns >0 — the smoking gun that the bug existed and was correctly identified. 6/6 pass. **Triple-check verification:** (1) PHP lint clean both files; (2) D131 gate green — parity smoke "PARITY OK" 7.0s + invariants smoke "INVARIANTS OK" (I1+I2+I3 untouched); (3) idempotent re-run of smoke (each run uses fresh template IDs since auto-increment moves forward; cleanup verified). **Bonus carry-forward (NOT addressed in this session):** `S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP` — the 3 UI dropdowns still submit template names from `<option value="<?= $t['name'] ?>">`. Net effect today is invisible (zero UI write activity), but a future operator using the form would silently write a row that lookup ignores. Fix requires UX decision: dedup the dropdown to show categories (one option per category with a friendly label) OR show template names but submit category values (visual ambiguity if 2 templates share a category). Out of scope here because it's a UX call, not a code fix. **NOT touched:** UI dropdowns (deferred to S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP); API validators at api/v1/customer_equipment_rates/upsert.php + api/v1/rate_cards/create.php (currently `clean_string` only, no enum validation — could add ENUM constraint when UI is fixed); seed scripts (already write correct category form); `FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql` (no schema changes — query semantic change only); `.env` / FF_ASSET_VERSION (server-side change, no asset cache implication); rate_card_history (no such table — rate_cards has audit_log only). **Carry-forward:** S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP (3 dropdowns + 2 API validators); separately, S-MILEAGE-RATE-VALIDATION (parallel to S-BILLING-RATE-FIX C2/C3/C4 defensive layers — already queued, runs next after this entry lands). **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **Docblock vs reality drift** — the lookup_rates.php docblock confidently asserted "rate_card_items.equipment_type and customer_equipment_rates.equipment_type both store this as a string matching the template name" (line 80-81 pre-fix). The docblock was the source of the bug: someone wrote the lookup matching the docblock's claim, but the actual data (written by separate seed scripts) used a different convention. The docblock had been wrong since seed and survived multiple passes through review. Treat docblocks as claims to verify against the data, not as authoritative spec — and when docblocks are corrected, write WHY the prior claim was wrong so the next reader knows the trap. (2) **Pre-work agent scope** — the Explore agent inventory found 14+ readers/writers in <600 words; the inline DB queries cross-checked the agent's assertions against actual data values. Combining the two (agent for breadth + DB for ground truth) is a reliable pattern when the question is "what value-space does this column actually hold". The agent on its own may misread variable names (the agent's "Decision" recommendation in this case proposed Option B based on the assumption that UI dropdowns submit template names — true, but it missed that the UI has zero live-write activity, which made Option A correct without UI changes). (3) **Smoke-test temp data discipline** — to test the Priority 3 + Priority 4 paths required temporary equipment_templates with category='other' (the only category with no rate_card_items entries). The smoke inserts both upfront, runs all 5 tests, deletes them in a finally block. Each run uses fresh auto-increment IDs (visible in the PASS lines as `tmpl_id=22, 23` then `24, 25` etc.) — that's the expected cost of test isolation; the cleanup is verified by `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM equipment_templates WHERE name LIKE '__SMOKE_LOOKUP_RATES%'` returning 0 post-run. |

(c) **Print emulation** via preview_eval — injected both @media print blocks as @media all in a `<style>` element, walked DOM for visible position:fixed elements with dark backgrounds + non-zero rect + ancestor-visibility; pre-fix scan reproduced the overlay (search-overlay rgba(0,0,0,0.5) + modal-backdrop rgba(0,0,0,0.7)), post-fix scan reports zero overlays across all 3 reference invoices. (d) **Operator visual T1 PASS** — confirmed after C3-T1-FIX deployed and `.env` FF_ASSET_VERSION bumped 1.0.25 → 1.0.26 (uncommitted, gitignored). **NOT touched**: api/v1/invoices/show.php (server-side load was sufficient; AJAX endpoint unaffected); FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql (no schema change); FLEETFORGE_SPEC_FINAL.md / FLEETFORGE_ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md (no spec-text change — display work is in DECISIONS table + REFERENCE.md only if needed); FLEETFORGE_DESIGN_DETAILS.md (no new design tokens — extends existing patterns); Mileage Review card + Odometer & Distance card + Rate Explanation card (D-E exclusion held — these are S-MILEAGE-2B territory). **Carry-forward**: (a) S-MILEAGE-2A inherits the line-item dispatch contract + dual S-MILEAGE-2B extension markers — no code reshape needed when adding `mileage_drawdown_credit` / `mileage_usage` line types, just config + match-case + template fragment; (b) S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX dormant tax-math bug (queued earlier in S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX) remains exercisable post-2A when Model B Lite flows through review approval; (c) production cache invalidation: production deploy needs FF_ASSET_VERSION 1.0.25 → 1.0.26 bump in production .env to invalidate cached app.css with old print hide list. **KEY LEARNINGS**: K-13 locked — global include CSS as universal print concern (see KEY LEARNINGS table). Secondary learnings inline: (1) **Pre-flight render emulation as auth-free visual proof** — PHP CLI render with faked $_SESSION + regex extraction of marker patterns produces lossless markup verification without needing real auth; combined with `preview_eval` CSS injection (@media print → @media all) gives screenshot-quality visual proof of print rendering, all under operator-controlled local execution. Cheaper than the K-1-class "share dev test user credentials" pattern when the verification is structural rather than interactive. (2) **Synthetic data via BEGIN/ROLLBACK as a test-pollution-free seam** — applies for any T1 that needs to verify a rendering against a data shape that doesn't yet exist in production data (`credit_note_applications` was empty at lock time). Pattern: insert in a transaction, render, validate, ROLLBACK, post-rollback verify no orphan rows. Matches the `tests/_stress_*.php` BEGIN/ROLLBACK pattern from S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX C1. (3) **Operator refinement on tooltip wording surfaces the right audit question** — my initial proposal "Applied to: line #1, #2, #4" forced the accountant to mentally cross-reference line numbers. Operator refinement "Applied to N taxable lines totaling $X" answers the actual reconciliation question ("does the tax base reconcile to the taxable subtotal?") in one read. Surfacing tooltip wording for sign-off rather than shipping the first draft prevented a UX-debt accumulation. |

Here GPS differs from insurance/warranty in two specific places (default opt_in true vs false, per-day billing vs flat-per-period); everything else matches verbatim. The pre-work surfacing of all 7 reference files BEFORE writing code prevented divergence by accident. Pattern: when adding a parallel feature, list every layer the existing feature touches, copy the exact form, then deliberately mark the divergences. Anything unmarked stays identical. (2) **K-9 — COMMENT clauses in migration DDL.** First migration apply produced a parity FAIL because the ADD COLUMN DDL strings omitted the COMMENT clause that master schema needs for documentation parity. The `ff_add_column_if_missing` helper short-circuits if the column already exists, so a re-run won't add the COMMENT after-the-fact. Fix pattern: include the COMMENT clause in the initial DDL string AND issue a separate idempotent `ALTER TABLE … MODIFY COLUMN … COMMENT` for the case where the column was already added in a prior dev iteration (or to fix up a partial application). When updating the file post-apply also update schema_migrations.checksum to match. The migration file pattern from S-MILEAGE-1 (precharge_*) used double-quoted DDL with single-quoted COMMENT — copy verbatim. (3) **K-10 — Operator confirmation on backfill default.** D-G presented two options: (i) default 1.00 on schema → all existing leases auto-bill $1/day; (ii) explicit UPDATE to 0.00 → existing leases preserved at no-billing. The original ticket's plan was option (ii). The user's "$1/day default" directive was ambiguous on backfill semantics. Surfaced the tradeoff explicitly with a recommendation (default ii); operator picked (i). Pattern: when a directive could plausibly mean either of two operationally-distinct outcomes (especially one that touches existing customer billing), surface both with stakes, recommend the safer default, let operator pick. The 3-line `Confirm (i) or (ii)?` prompt was the right cost for the decision. |

The earlier classification was technically defensible from the code's perspective but missed the operator's mental model. Pattern: when classifying an ambiguous shape, surface the proposed disposition before writing fix code — operator may have a different model than the code's. Reconciliation: trust the latest committed state when it's correct; delete duplicates locally; document the reconciliation explicitly in the SESSION LOG. The D131 gate ran clean post-reconciliation, validating the merged state. Pattern: when discovering parallel agent work, verify smoke gates pass on the combined state before continuing — don't blindly revert or rewrite. (4) **K-7 — Engine fix vs. defensive layer trade-off.** D133 added defensive validation to reject (allowance>0 + rate=0) at lease-create time. D135 takes the opposite approach for the (allowance=0 + rate>0) shape: instead of rejecting at create-time, FIX the engine to process the shape correctly. The choice between "reject upstream" vs "process correctly" hinges on whether the shape represents real business intent. When it does, reject is wrong; when it doesn't, reject is correct. This session: rate>0 + allowance=0 IS real intent ("bill every km"), so engine fix is correct; rate=0 + allowance>0 is NOT real intent ("operator forgot to set rate"), so reject is correct. |

Lease 52 duplicate-INV-89/90 anomaly noted but not auto-resolved — operator's call (likely covered by S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP-style cleanup or routine void). **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **K-2 — Diagnostic-first protocol for ambiguous bug-vs-correct-behavior.** When an operator flags "X looks wrong" without a clear classification, structure the pre-work to disambiguate three branches before writing code: (a) REAL BUG — math says one thing, code does another → fix; (b) CORRECT BEHAVIOR misunderstood as bug → document + improve visualization; (c) VALIDATION GAP — code is internally consistent but a data shape it doesn't anticipate falls through silently → upstream guard. The classification is a 15-minute investigation that determines whether you're shipping a bug fix, a docs commit, or a queued follow-up. Skipping the diagnostic and jumping to "fix the symptom" risks fixing the wrong layer (e.g. patching InvoiceGenerator when the real fix is at lease create-time). Mirrors the diagnostic protocol used in S-MILEAGE-MODEL-AUDIT and S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE. (2) **K-3 — Defensive auto-fill guards surface anomalies cleanly.** The C2 over-invoiced anomaly guard (`period_start > ceiling`) was added to handle a hypothetical edge case during stress testing — but it actually surfaces a real anomaly in production data (lease 52's duplicate INV-89/90). The operator sees a clear warning at the form ("prior invoice ended past lease ceiling — manual review needed") instead of producing an invalid period_start > period_end. Pattern: when auto-fill logic encounters impossible combinations of inputs, prefer to skip + warn over silently producing nonsense, even if the input combination "shouldn't happen." The guard becomes both a UX improvement and a debugging aid. |

Optional future polish: (a) harden the alternate mileage-line-item insert paths in review_mileage.php + close.php with the same throw — low priority because those are operator-mediated paths; (b) S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP per KNOWN ISSUES A4 — lease 21 has multiple data anomalies (A2 INV-84 period outside lease span; A4 same-day create→close suggests seed/test data); voids alone close I5 but leave the underlying lease state for later cleanup → RESOLVED 2026-05-13 via S-LEASE-21-CLEANUP (KI #107, disposition C — seed/test data); (c) S-RATES-UI-CATEGORY-DEDUP from S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE carry-forward (3 dropdowns + 2 API validators); (d) consider extending D130 wording to cover scope CONTRACTION explicitly per K-NEXT KEY LEARNING below. **KEY LEARNINGS:** (1) **K-NEXT — Silent scope contraction is a recurring discipline gap.** S-MILEAGE-RATE-ZERO-FIX C1 contracted scope twice (dropped smoke gate work AND dropped INV-27/INV-84 voids) without explicit operator re-authorization or SESSION LOG diff at the moment of contraction. Both pieces surfaced later as "discoveries" in S-MILEAGE-RATE-VALIDATION pre-work + I5 trip. Per D130 spirit (currently scoped to expansion, broaden to contraction): any mid-session scope change requires explicit operator re-authorization + SESSION LOG note at the moment it happens, not retrospective recovery in a future session. The retrospective recovery worked here because both pieces were caught quickly (same day) by the next session's pre-work + smoke gate, but the discipline gap means neither catch was guaranteed — different gating could have shipped silent under-billing to a customer. Consider extending D130 wording to cover contraction explicitly: "any mid-session scope change (expansion OR contraction) requires explicit operator re-authorization + SESSION LOG note at the moment it happens". This applies to ALL sessions going forward. (2) **HARD-vs-SOFT split for two-mode failure** — D-B (throw) and D-C (warning) reflect two distinct failure modes for the same observable symptom (mileage block produces no charge). Allowance configured + rate=0 = data hole that demands fail-loud (the D132-class bug pattern). No allowance configured + rate=0 + distance recorded = possible misconfiguration that's also a legitimate "no per-km billing" state (operator chose not to bill mileage on this lease). Mixing the two into a single throw would over-trigger on the legitimate case; the soft signal (Sentry warning + audit_log) is the right severity for the ambiguous state. The pattern: when refusing-to-execute would block legitimate operator intent, downgrade to warn-and-continue with a clear diagnostic the operator can investigate. (3) **Reuse existing exception via context array** — `BillingRateException`'s constructor was billing-tier-specific (method/daily/weekly/monthly) but its `$context` field is the extension point. Mileage-specific fields (estimated_mileage_km, mileage_rate_km, period_distance_km) fit cleanly without a constructor change. The class stays cohesive (one exception type for "billing rate failed") rather than spawning a sibling MileageBillingException; the `method` discriminator (`'mileage_excess'`) lets log readers grep for the new case without ambiguity. When extending an existing exception class, prefer the context array over constructor changes. (4) **Stage-split a multi-condition gate to attach a throw** — the original gate was a single 4-condition AND; refactoring it into "expected" (3 conditions) + "rate check" (1 condition) made the throw natural. The pattern: when adding a throw to silent-skip code, find the conditions that mean "this code SHOULD run" and the conditions that mean "this code can run safely" — the throw goes between them. The split makes the intent explicit and is a one-line readability win even without the throw. |

| S-RATELIMITER-TZ-FIX | 2026-05-17 | bugfix | Fixed the RateLimiter clock-skew bug that made `threshold > 0` settings unusable in environments where MySQL system_time_zone differs from PHP's `date_default_timezone_get()`. **Surfaced during operator triage:** "Too many sign-in attempts from your network" lockout that wouldn't clear even with `security.rate_limit.login_ip_threshold = 0` / `window_minutes = 0` / `block_minutes = 0` in `settings`. **Root cause:** `lib/Security/RateLimiter.php` stored `window_start` and `blocked_until` via MySQL `NOW()` under the session timezone set by `includes/db.php:65` (`SET time_zone = '+00:00'`, i.e. UTC) — but compared those columns against `time()` via `strtotime((string) $row['window_start'])`. `strtotime()` parses bare `Y-m-d H:i:s` strings in PHP's default timezone (`APP_TIMEZONE = America/Vancouver`), so a UTC string like `2026-05-16 19:21:11` got interpreted as Vancouver-local — shifting it ~7h into the future relative to `time()`. Result: `($now - $windowStartTs)` was always negative, the "window expired" branch never fired, and every attempt past the first one fell into the increment-and-check path and tripped the threshold (which trips at `newCount > 0` when threshold=0). Same incident on the write side — `date('Y-m-d H:i:s', $now + $blockMinutes * 60)` emitted Vancouver-local strings that MySQL stored verbatim under +00:00, making blocked windows appear ~7h longer than configured. The bug compounded on systems with even larger MySQL/PHP timezone deltas (operator's MySQL `@@system_time_zone` was IST, a 12.5h delta — but the +00:00 session override masked that for read paths going through the app). **Fix (`lib/Security/RateLimiter.php`):** moved all timestamp comparison into Unix-epoch integer space. SELECT now reads `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(window_start) AS window_start_ts` and `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(blocked_until) AS blocked_until_ts` (returns NULL for NULL columns — null check still works). Read paths cast to `(int)` and compare against `time()` directly. Write path passes the Unix timestamp via `FROM_UNIXTIME(?)` — `FROM_UNIXTIME(NULL) → NULL` preserves the "no block window" branch. No `strtotime()` or `date()` formatting remain in the timestamp paths; timezone-agnostic by construction. **Regression test:** `tests/_stress_rate_limiter_tz.php` (NEW — 7 test groups / 14 assertions covering: first-attempt row creation, in-window increment, threshold crossing → block, block honored on subsequent request, backdated `window_start` → reset (T5 — the specific assertion the bug was killing pre-fix), backdated `blocked_until` → ignored as expired, `reset()` clears row). 14/14 PASS. Pre-fix, T5 + T6 would have failed because `strtotime()` shifted the backdated DB string forward by the PHP↔UTC delta, making `($now - $windowStartTs)` look like a small positive instead of "1 hour ago in epoch space". **Verified live:** simulated 5 sequential `RateLimiter::check()` calls against `login:ip:127.0.0.1` with the operator's current `threshold=0/window=0/block=0` settings — all 5 returned `allowed=true` (threshold=0 + window=0 now correctly behaves as "limiter disabled"; pre-fix it behaved as "block on attempt 2"). PHP syntax clean on the patched file and the new test. **Operator action immediately preceding this fix:** cleared the stale `login:ip:127.0.0.1` row in `rate_limit_attempts` + reset `users.id=1.login_attempts` to 0 (so the operator could log in with the new password set in the same session). **Not touched:** the `rate_limit_attempts` schema; the call sites in `app/auth/login.php` + `app/auth/mfa_challenge.php` + `app/auth/forgot_password.php` + AI endpoints (signature unchanged — the fix is purely internal to `RateLimiter::check()`). **Other places that compare `time()` against DB DATETIME columns via `strtotime()` may have the same class of bug** and were NOT audited in this session — `grep -rn "strtotime(.*\[" lib/ includes/ api/` is the diagnostic, queued as a follow-up if the operator hits another timezone-shaped symptom. Single-commit arc (no IN-FLIGHT registration — incident response). |

The dev box where this commit was made is safe (rm --cached preserved the files there by construction). PHP not touched; schema not touched; no migrations; pure index/gitignore hygiene. Single-commit code arc (d62d469) + docs commit (this entry). |
| S-BILLING-HOLISTIC-ENGINE | 2026-05-17 | feature | Replaces ProRateCalculator's period-independent THE LAW with a holistic running-reconciliation engine for new leases. **Boss's bug:** old engine bills each period in isolation, so a lease that crosses tier boundaries (e.g. 4-day partial month + 30-day full month at $50/$350/$700) overcharges by $106.67 ($900 vs the correct $793.33) because it can't see the future tier when computing the activation invoice. **Algorithm (spec §3, §7):** every invoice answers the same 5 questions — (1) inclusive day count start_date→period_end; (2) tier (1-5 daily / 6-7 weekly_flat / 8-29 weekly_math capped at monthly / 30+ monthly_math — same THE LAW thresholds); (3) cumulative_correct = applyTierFormula(total_days); (4) already_billed = SUM(base_rental from prior non-void invoices, net of any prior reconciliation credits); (5) delta = cumulative_correct − already_billed. Positive delta → emit `base_rental` line; zero → emit nothing; negative → emit `base_rental_reconciliation_credit` with POSITIVE amount + is_credit=1 (K-16 convention — matches mileage_drawdown_credit shape; aggregator subtracts; per-line tax negates via bcmul sign-propagation in TaxCalculator). **Activation special case (spec §17):** Invoice 1 (already_billed=0) applies "whichever pays more" — bills the HIGHER of (current-tier formula for period days) vs (period_days × monthly/30). Protects the company against quick returns on long-term-priced leases. The engine confirms activation against ground truth (the SUM query) so the caller's `is_activation_invoice` guess can't accidentally fire the rule on a 2nd+ invoice. **6 migrations (all naturally idempotent via append-at-end ENUM, ff_add_column_if_missing helper, or INSERT IGNORE):** 0100 invoice audit columns (`total_days_at_period_end` INT, `cumulative_correct_amount` DECIMAL(12,2), `already_billed_before_this` DECIMAL(12,2) — NULL for period_independent leases + pre-engine invoices), 0101 invoice_line_items.item_type ENUM +1 (`base_rental_reconciliation_credit`; ENUM grows 16→17, all existing values preserved verified live), 0102 credit_notes.source ENUM +1 (`base_rental_reconciliation_overflow`; 8→9 values), 0103 leases.engine_version ENUM ('period_independent','holistic') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'holistic', 0104 lock_existing_to_old (UPDATE 23 active+pending leases to period_independent; audit_log row records the count), 0105 settings flag `billing.engine_version=holistic` is_public=0 (paper spec said is_editable — that column doesn't exist on the live settings table; used is_public per actual schema). **Engine class** `lib/Billing/HolisticLeaseEngine.php` (~430 lines) — pure-math + ONE read query (the already_billed SUM); no DB writes (D3: InvoiceGenerator is sole writer). Methods exactly per spec §30.1: `calculateForInvoice(array): array`, `applyTierFormula(int,string,string,string): array` (public, reusable), `whicheverPaysMore(int,string,string,string): array` (public — exposed for unit-testability vs spec's "private"), `inclusiveDays(string,string): int` (static). Throws BillingRateException at engine boundary for D132 zero-rate-with-period-days. **InvoiceGenerator wiring** (`lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php`) — constructor instantiates HolisticLeaseEngine alongside ProRateCalculator. createFromLease()'s Step 1 block now branches on `lease.engine_version`: holistic → calculateForInvoice() + emit engine's chosen line type (base_rental OR base_rental_reconciliation_credit OR none) + populate the three audit columns + write `audit_log` entity_type='invoice_holistic_reconciliation' row with full audit_meta JSON; period_independent → unchanged ProRateCalculator path. Holistic path uses `FOR UPDATE` on the lease row (D20) for the already_billed read so concurrent invoice generation serializes. The legacy D132 backstop is bypassed on the holistic path (engine throws its own); the legacy is_activation determination is replaced by ground-truth (already_billed===0). **rate_method mapping helper** added (`mapTierToRateMethod`) — engine's richer tier vocabulary ('weekly_flat','weekly_math','weekly_capped','monthly_math') collapses to invoices.rate_method_used ENUM ('daily','weekly','weekly_capped','monthly','none'). **Overflow handler extended (spec §19.2, Step 4):** the existing S-FIX-2 Bug #3 cap mechanism now accepts EITHER `mileage_credit` OR `base_rental_reconciliation_credit` as the cappable line (priority order: mileage_credit first to preserve pre-existing byte-for-byte behavior). The credit_notes.source is chosen accordingly — `mileage_overpayment` vs `base_rental_reconciliation_overflow` — and the reason/audit_log notes branch on the source. **Tests** `tests/_stress_holistic_engine.php` — 88 / 88 pass. Coverage: unit tests for every tier boundary (Appendix A), whicheverPaysMore (A wins, B wins, tie), inclusiveDays (leap years, year boundaries, inverted ranges); integration tests for boss's exact 34-day example (Invoice 1 $200, Invoice 2 $593.33, total $793.33), day 5/6/7/8/14 closes (tier crossings), leap year Feb 1-29 (29 days = $700 capped), 365-day annual lease, full 6-month sequence (138-day cumulative $3,220.00), negative-delta with overflow → credit_notes row, holistic audit_log row present; regression tests confirming period_independent still uses ProRateCalculator and never emits a reconciliation_credit line and never populates the audit columns. **Spec §35.7 precision band:** days 65/365/366 differ from Appendix A's display values by $0.02 — Appendix A uses pre-rounded $23.33 × N; engine uses bcdiv($monthly,'30',6) × N per spec §7.2 pseudocode (matches ProRateCalculator). Boss already approved this 2-cent tolerance in §35.7. **Adjacent regression suites pass:** _stress_billing_rate_exception 11/11, _stress_invoice_generator_precharge 6/6, _stress_drawdown_emit 6/6, _smoke_billing_invariants I1-I10 OK, _smoke_master_schema_parity PARITY OK after audit-column repositioning in master to match ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN's at-end placement. **bin/migrate.php** dry-run showed exactly 6 pending (stop condition #6 met); apply 6/6 in 675ms total; verify 25 ok / 0 drift / 0 missing. **Migration impact:** 23 active+pending leases locked to period_independent (they continue billing on the old engine until close — mid-lease engine switch would invalidate prior invoices' math per spec §32); 8 closed leases received the new default 'holistic' (harmless — they won't generate further invoices). **Open Questions resolved at build time (spec §35):** §35.1 confirmed (whichever-pays-more at activation only); §35.2 Option A (lock existing); §35.3 activation = already_billed===0 ground truth (caller may guess via billing_type, engine vetoes); §35.5 rate-change-on-active still prohibited at policy layer (not enforced in this session — engine math would reconcile but audit trail murky); §35.6 same-day = 1 day inclusive (verified in inclusiveDays test); §35.7 2-cent precision band accepted per existing boss approval. **Deviation:** spec §30.1 marked `whicheverPaysMore` private; exposed as public to enable direct unit-testability — no behavior change. spec §29.4 settings row used is_editable which doesn't exist on the live settings table; used is_public=0 (admin-only) per actual schema. spec §7.3 `SUM(li.amount) WHERE item_type='base_rental'` extended to include `base_rental_reconciliation_credit` with signed-aggregate semantics so the running already_billed never double-counts a prior reconciliation. **3-step feature arc:** migrations (0100-0105) + engine class + InvoiceGenerator wiring + tests + master parity reposition all land in one commit per the spec's "Build silently. No previews. No partial reports between steps." discipline. |

Reference = `LSE-DF-INC-{contract_number}`. **Part C — EXTENDED method `onLeasePeriodPosting_Capital`** (D-LESSOR-4-PERIOD-EXTENDED supersedes D-LESSOR-3-PERIOD-GENERIC): the method is generic in interface (still accepts sales_type AND direct_financing classifications, same signature) but classification-aware in implementation. Sales-type periods keep the 3-line LESSOR-3 NET-method shape unchanged (preserves the regression-safe contract). DF periods detect `initial_direct_costs > 0` and add a 4th JE line `CR Deferred IDC` + reduce the Finance Income line by the same amount. Per-period IDC amort = `initial_direct_costs / termMonths` (bcmath scale=2 straight-line slice, locked via D-LESSOR-4-IDC-AMORT-STRAIGHT-LINE). Last regular period (`period_number === termMonths`) absorbs the rounding tail: `priorAmort = SUM(jel.credit) WHERE source_type='lease_period' AND source_id=lease AND account_id=deferred_idc`, then `thisAmort = initial_direct_costs − priorAmort`. BPO period (`period_number > termMonths`) gets `idcAmort = $0.00` — IDC fully amortized by end of regular term. Defensive: warns (error_log) when IDC amort > finance for a period (produces negative adjusted_finance, which the JE renders as `DR Finance Income` — mathematically valid revenue reduction, unusual but accepted); negative principal_corrected guard. Term lookup from acc_lease_classifications.criterion_b_lease_term_months. Cron at cron/accounting_recurring_entries.php already includes `WHERE l.classification IN ('sales_type','direct_financing')` (from LESSOR-3), so DF leases flow through the existing batch loop without any cron-side change. **Part D — wiring**: api/v1/leases/activate.php (UPDATE) — existing LESSOR-3 sales_type inception hook extended with `elseif ($classification === 'direct_financing')` branch that calls `AutoEntryBridge::onLeaseInception_DirectFinancing`. Both bridge methods gate on `accounting.lessor_module_enabled='1'` (LESSOR-1 setting, default '0'). Non-fatal try/catch — activation always succeeds, JE failure logs + attaches `inception_je: {posted:false, error:...}` to response. close.php and cron unchanged (onLeaseTermination + the period batch already handle both classifications per LESSOR-3). **Functional smoke** (`/tmp/lessor4_smoke.php`, live rollback): 5/5 PASS — (1) DF inception lease #1 (FA #1, carrying $48,430 = $58,000 − $9,570 accum dep), FV=$47,430, IDC=$1,000, term=60mo. Schedule generated (60 regular + 1 BPO, annual rate 53.14%). Inception JE #1141 (5 lines): DR NI_cur $2,212.15 + DR NI_lt $45,217.85 + DR Deferred IDC $1,000 + DR AccDep $9,570 + CR AssetCost $58,000 = $58,000 balanced ✅. No COGS line ✅. No Sales Revenue line ✅. Asset #1.status='disposed' ✅. (2) DF period 1 JE #1142 (4 lines, balanced $2,200 DR=CR): idc_amort=$16.66 (= $1,000/60 bcdiv truncated), adjusted_finance=$2,039.70, Deferred IDC credit line present ✅. (3) Rounding tail: posted periods 2..60 sequentially; Σ amort accumulator = $1,000.00 in-memory AND $1,000.00 in DB query (=Σ credits on account #93 source_type='lease_period' source_id=1) — EXACTLY equals initial IDC of $1,000 ✅. Period 60 absorbs the rounding via `thisAmort = $1000 − sum(prior amorts)` formula. (4) Sales-type regression: lease #2 inception + period 1 — period JE still has 3 lines (no Deferred IDC leak), `idc_amort=0.00` ✅. The sales_type path is byte-identical to LESSOR-3 behavior, confirmed empirically. (5) BPO period (period 61 of DF lease): idc_amort=$0.00 ✅, no Deferred IDC line on JE ✅. | S-PERM-SESSION-REFRESH | 2026-05-20 | infrastructure/perm-hygiene | **Stale-session UX fix** — closes the open hazard from `audits/2026-05-20_permission_audit.md` §6 and the Q1 question dismissed during S-PERM-MACRO-STATUS triage. Symptom: super_admin grants overrides on a target user who's already logged in; target's `can()` reads from `$_SESSION['ff_user']['permission_overrides']` snapshot from THEIR login time, doesn't see the new overrides, gets stale 403/200 mismatch. Required log-out + log-in to take effect. Now fixed: target's next authenticated request auto-refreshes the in-session map via a timestamp comparison. **4 decisions locked**: D-PERM-REFRESH-1 (per-request timestamp comparison, static $checked cache within the request — at most 1 extra SELECT per authenticated page), D-PERM-REFRESH-2 (3 write endpoints stamp `users.permissions_updated_at = NOW()`; login does NOT stamp), D-PERM-REFRESH-3 (stale = DB.timestamp > session.timestamp OR session.timestamp IS NULL while DB.timestamp is set), D-PERM-REFRESH-4 (super_admin sessions skip the freshness check entirely — they short-circuit `can()` regardless of overrides). **Migration** `db_migrations/202605200400_S-PERM-SESSION-REFRESH.sql` (43→44/0/0): ALTER `users` ADD COLUMN `permissions_updated_at TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT NULL AFTER mfa_verified_until`. No index (single-row PK lookup pattern). Existing users get NULL (no prior change) so their freshness check short-circuits until the first override change. FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql synced (column inserted after mfa_verified_until in the `users` CREATE TABLE block); PARITY OK post-sync. **Part B — new function `_ff_check_permission_freshness()` in includes/auth.php** (~60 lines added next to `_ff_refresh_user_permissions()`): static `$checked` flag for one-shot-per-request; early-return on missing `$_SESSION['ff_user']['id']` (protects cron/CLI scripts that include auth.php); early-return for super_admin (D-PERM-REFRESH-4); fetches `users.permissions_updated_at` via single PK lookup (used `db_row()['col']` — `db_value()` doesn't exist in the codebase, the session prompt got the helper name wrong; trust file over prompt); compares via `strtotime()` against `$_SESSION['ff_user']['permissions_loaded_at']`; if stale, re-loads overrides via `_ff_load_user_overrides()` directly (bypasses the `current_user_id() !== $userId` guard inside `_ff_refresh_user_permissions()` — by definition the freshness check runs under the target's own session, but the direct write makes the contract self-documenting). **Bootstrap wiring** — the session prompt assumed an `includes/init.php` exists but the codebase has no such file. The canonical per-request auth hooks are `require_auth()` (page) + `require_auth_api()` (API), called by 124 + 416 = **540 endpoints** combined. Added a single `_ff_check_permission_freshness();` call at the bottom of each function after the existing `current_user()` check. **`auth_login()` updated** (~line 233) to also set `$_SESSION['ff_user']['permissions_loaded_at'] = date('Y-m-d H:i:s')` alongside the existing override loading — establishes the session-side timestamp for the comparison. **Part D — 3 write endpoints stamp `users.permissions_updated_at = NOW()`** INSIDE the existing `db_transaction()` (atomic with the override row mutation + audit_log insert): `api/v1/users/permissions/update.php` (single-cell, stamps once at end of transaction), `api/v1/users/permissions/group_apply.php` (bulk macro, stamps **ONCE at end of macro loop** not per-cell — D-PERM-REFRESH-2 — from the target's perspective a bulk macro is a single "permissions changed" event, so N override writes + 1 timestamp update covers the auto-refresh signal cleanly), `api/v1/users/permissions/reset.php` (full reset, stamps once after DELETE). **Touched files (6 modified + 1 new):** db_migrations/202605200400_S-PERM-SESSION-REFRESH.sql (NEW), FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql (sync), includes/auth.php (new function + require_auth/require_auth_api hooks + auth_login set loaded_at), api/v1/users/permissions/update.php (stamp), api/v1/users/permissions/group_apply.php (stamp), api/v1/users/permissions/reset.php (stamp). **PHP lint clean** on all. **Functional smoke** (HTTP-driven, temporary password reset on users 23 + 25, restored byte-identical post-test): **7/7 smoke tests PASS** plus T3 verified by inspection. T1 (baseline): dispatcher logged in, users.permissions_updated_at=NULL, /accounting/dashboard → 403 ✅. T2 (the core fix — stale-session detection + auto-refresh): dispatcher logged in (cookie jar D), super_admin (cookie jar SA) grants journal_entries.view=1 → users.permissions_updated_at stamped to NOW(). Dispatcher hits /accounting/dashboard with the STALE cookie → **HTTP 200** (_ff_check_permission_freshness fired, refreshed the session, can() now sees the override) ✅. T4 (idempotent reload): re-hit returns 200 with no extra refresh (DB stamp not newer than session stamp now) ✅. T5 (super_admin skip): super_admin → /dashboard 200 (their freshness check short-circuits) ✅. T6 (reset endpoint stamps + propagates): SA POST /reset.php → users.permissions_updated_at updates → dispatcher's next /accounting/dashboard → 403 (revoked override propagates immediately) ✅. T7 (group macro stamps ONCE): SA POST /group_apply.php with macro=grant_view on accounting → 10 overrides created + single timestamp update (not 10) ✅. T8 (cron isolation): `php cron/accounting_lease_ni_reclass.php` exit 0, no crash from the new function (the `!isset($_SESSION['ff_user']['id'])` guard short-circuits in CLI context) ✅. T3 by inspection: the static `$checked` flag in `_ff_check_permission_freshness()` ensures at most one DB hit per PHP request; multiple `require_auth()` calls within the same process (rare but possible) chain through the cached state without re-querying. **D131 6/6 PASS** post-commit (PARITY OK + I1-I10 + samsara 16/16 + model_b 20/20 + doc_freshness 17/17 + migrate 44/0/0). **Cost analysis**: 1 extra `SELECT permissions_updated_at FROM users WHERE id = ?` per authenticated request for non-super_admin users. Single-row primary-key lookup, no index needed (PK is the index), negligible. For super_admin (~4 users on disk) zero overhead — their freshness check returns before the SELECT. For users with `permissions_updated_at IS NULL` (never had an override change) the function returns after the SELECT but before the strtotime comparison — single-row lookup only. **No regressions**: 1 K-22 catch — session prompt referenced `includes/init.php` which doesn't exist; codebase uses `require_auth()` + `require_auth_api()` as the hook points instead. 1 prompt-vs-file mismatch — session prompt referenced `db_value()` helper which doesn't exist; used `db_row()['col']` pattern (the canonical helper in this codebase). Both adjustments silent per [[feedback_trust_file_over_prompt]]. **Resolves**: `audits/2026-05-20_permission_audit.md` §6 stale-session UX hazard; closes the dismissed Q1 follow-up from the S-PERM-MACRO-STATUS triage. |

Two bugs fixed — both debt-paydown; does not advance Phase QBO count.** **Bug F2 (blocker — silent CAD→USD currency coercion, D-QBO-FIXPACK-1/-2):** InvoicePusher.buildQboPayload previously omitted CurrencyRef entirely for CAD invoices (D-QBO-11-3 "CAD omits CurrencyRef" FX block); QBO deferred to the mapped customer's home currency — for CAD invoices mapped to a USD QBO customer, the QBO Invoice was silently recorded in USD. | S-QBO-MATCHER-WEDGE-RECOVERY | 2026-05-27 | quickbooks/matcher-wedge-recovery | **Closed the wedged half-state recovery gap** surfaced in S-QBO-LIVE-VERIFY-RERUN-2026-05-26 (row 4302 required manual 1-line UPDATE to link FF 1030 → QBO #84). The wedge class: `mapping_status='ff_only'` + `qbo_*_id IS NULL` + QBO breadcrumb columns populated (residue from prior pull→unlink). Standard matcher cascade can't reach these (UPDATE uses `WHERE qbo_*_id=?` which NULL never matches). All 5 Matchers (Account/Customer/Vendor/TaxCode/Item) gain a private `rescueHalfStateRows()` method called as **Pass 0** of `matchAll()`. Algorithm: SELECT wedged rows → for each, look up matching qbo_only row by breadcrumb (preferred field then fallback per entity type) → if matched, DELETE qbo_only candidate FIRST (clears UNIQUE constraint) → UPDATE wedge row to absorb qbo_*_id + sync_token + breadcrumb metadata, flip mapping_status='mapped' + match_confidence='high' + match_notes='wedge_recovery: linked by <field>'. Claimed qbo_ids flow into the standard `$matchedQboIds` set so the subsequent cascade doesn't double-claim (D-MATCHER-CLAIMED-SET preserved). Added `GET_LOCK('ff_cron_ai_anomaly_scan', 0)` (naming convention `ff_cron_<filename>`; runbook's `ff_cron_ai_anomaly` was wrong — aligned to code convention), start + end `audit_log` rows (matching archive_old_data.php + reconcile_counters.php pattern), and `finally` RELEASE_LOCK. ' UTC')` → ~7-8h error in `$hoursSince` vs the >8h offline threshold → false/suppressed offline alerts. Fix: resolved `settings.company.timezone` once outside the unit loop into a `$alertTz` (`DateTimeZone`), then used `DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('Y-m-d H:i:s', $lastConn, $alertTz)->getTimestamp()` for the diff — same approach as HIGH-1 billing cron (D-BILLING-CRON-TZ). Latent (triggers only when a `manual_trigger` row ages past 365 days; 0 such rows today). Migration `202606030000` adds `'manual_trigger'` to `audit_log_archive.action` (mirrors the full `audit_log.action` definition exactly: same charset/collate/NOT NULL). DATABASE_MASTER synced; parity clean. | S-FIX-FLEETFORGE-C | 2026-06-07 | deploy/opcache-redeclare-window | **Prod compile fatal FLEETFORGE-C "Cannot redeclare help_button() (previously declared in includes/functions.php:772)" right after the fa497e27 deploy — diagnosed as a TRANSIENT opcache deploy-window redeclare, NOT a code duplicate.** Investigation (prod + repo): exactly ONE `help_button()` declaration (functions.php:772); functions.php loaded via `require_once` behind config/app.php's `defined('FF_LOADED')` re-entry guard; no second functions.php on disk; clean tree, no conflict markers; booting the real bootstrap + the help-drawer partial on prod runs clean; site healthy (dashboard 302). The fatal naming functions.php:772 as BOTH the prior AND throw site = signature of the SAME file compiled twice. Root cause: `bin/deploy.sh` does `git pull` in-place (step 4) while php-fpm serves; opcache (`validate_timestamps=On`, `revalidate_freq=2`) only clears at the step-8 reload, so a request in the pull→migrate→reload window compiles the freshly-pulled functions.php against stale opcode → redeclare; self-heals at reload. Deliberately did NOT remove a (nonexistent) duplicate or paper over with `function_exists()` (operator-forbidden). **Fix:** wrapped the pull→reload window in maintenance mode — `bin/deploy.sh` flips `MAINTENANCE_MODE=true` in `.env` before `git pull`, back to `false` after the fpm reload (opcache cleared) + before the health gate; `.env` is gitignored (pull never clobbers) + runtime-read (not opcode-cached) so the toggle is immediate; web gets 503 for the window, CLI steps unaffected; fail-CLOSED EXIT trap leaves maintenance on if the deploy aborts mid-window + prints how to clear. Dry-run confirmed ordering (ON→pull→migrate→reload→OFF→health). **Gate gap closed:** NEW `tests/_smoke_bootstrap_boot.php` 3/3 — P1 static-asserts no procedural function declared twice across includes/+config/ (non-vacuous: injected dup fails P1 pinpointing both sites), P2 boots config/app.php + help-drawer partial + calls help_button() (fails on any runtime fatal/redeclare); catches the class `php -l` misses. **Doc inventory:** PROGRESS SESSION LOG (this row, backfilled) + CURRENT_SESSIONS SHIPPED. **DEPLOY NOTE:** ff-deploy runs prod's CURRENT (un-gated) deploy.sh; it pulls the gated version but the gate protects the NEXT deploy — `git pull` bin/deploy.sh on prod first to gate this very deploy. **Commits:** `86bbb3f` (specific-path: bin/deploy.sh + smoke; docs backfilled in the S-INTEL-BRIEF-SEND-NOW commit). | D131 **green** (bash -n OK; dry-run gate ordering OK; new smoke 3/3 + non-vacuous) | decisions: none (deploy hardening; no literal duplicate existed). |

| S-BILLING-HOLISTIC-GENERATE-FIX | 2026-06-07 | billing/holistic-engine-revision-2 | **Revision 2 of the Holistic Lease Billing Engine — calendar-month billing, per-month fan-out, and manual-generation auto-fill repair. Fixes prod over-invoicing on the first real lease (#2620 MTTS-S667CV-2026, $100/$500/$1,500, Jun 7 → end_date Jul 7).** **Root causes (diagnosed against the live DB):** (1) the engine's monthly tier used **30-day-block math** (`floor(total/30)` months + `total%30 × monthly/30`) which charged a 31-day month an extra day and never aligned to calendar months; (2) the engine was **blind to the lease's known extent E** — it classified the tier off `period_end`, so it couldn't prorate a known span (`end_date` set) immediately; (3) **no per-calendar-month fan-out** on the manual/activation path (a single `createFromLease` per submitted period); (4) the **§17 "whichever pays more"** activation rule over-billed the first partial month (lease #2620's activation billed June flat $1,500 instead of the prorated $1,200); (5) the create-form auto-fill hit a **fully-invoiced edge** (latest non-void invoice at the ceiling → Period Start past ceiling → empty end / 0 days) and used a `+1 month −1 day` window (Jun 7→Jul 6) instead of the calendar-month boundary (Jun 30). **Fix — `lib/Billing/HolisticLeaseEngine.php`:** new `cumulativeCorrect(start, throughDate, E, rates)` replaces the 30-day-block monthly math — classify the regime on the duration through E (rate-driven crossover `weeklyMath(total) > monthly`, never a hardcoded day count); sub-month ladder (daily ≤5 / weekly_flat 6-7 / weekly_math) preserved and grown by days-through-`period_end`; **monthly applies → single calendar month bills flat monthly (28/29/30/31 — "a month is a month"), spanning bills per calendar-month segment (complete months flat, partial start/end months × monthly÷30)**. New helpers `weeklyMath()`, `sumSegments()`, `segmentsFor()` (fan-out plan), `sameCalendarMonth()`. `calculateForInvoice()` now takes `extent_end` (E), drops the wpm branch (R2 supersedes §17), emits the same audit JSON shape + `extent_end`/`basis`/`segments`. `applyTierFormula()`/`whicheverPaysMore()` retained as pure-math utilities (still unit-tested) but OFF the billing path. **`lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php`:** holistic branch resolves `extent_end = actual_return ?? end_date ?? period_end` and passes it; new **`generateForLease()` orchestrator** fans out one invoice per calendar-month segment for the spanning-monthly case (short/weekly/single-month → ONE `single_period` invoice; non-holistic/mileage_only → legacy single invoice), all in ONE `db_transaction` (atomic batch §11), each segment FOR UPDATE on the lease row, numbering D15; new `assertNoOverlap()` gate (§11 duplicate-period + void-before-regenerate immutability message, allow_overlap bypass, mileage_only exempt); `mapTierToRateMethod()` maps the new `monthly` tier. **`api/v1/invoices/create.php`:** calls `generateForLease`, emits one audit_log + notification per produced invoice, response carries `fanned`/`invoice_count`/`invoices[]`. **`app/admin/invoices/create.php`:** `_autoFillPeriodDatesFromCtx` rewritten — Period End = **last calendar day of Period Start's month** capped at the ceiling (replaces the removed `_addOneMonthMinusOneDay`); pre-fills Billing Type (`_segmentBillingType`) + Invoice Type (final when reaching the ceiling) per §10; **fully-invoiced edge now states "fully billed through &lt;date&gt;", shows the lease's own dates (not future-start/empty/0-days), and surfaces the void-then-regenerate recovery** (`fullyBilled` flag). **TEST COVERAGE (per-path, T1–T10):** NEW `tests/_smoke_holistic_generate_fix.php` **46/46** exercises the real `generateForLease`→`createFromLease`→DB path in BEGIN/ROLLBACK: T1 ladder 1d=$100·5d=$500·7d=$500·8d=$571.43·14d=$1,000·21d=$1,500·22d=$1,500·30d=$1,500; T2 spanning end_date Jul 7 → exactly TWO invoices (Jun 7-30 partial_start $1,200/24d + Jul 1-7 partial_end FINAL $350/7d; total $1,550); T3 prorate-in-the-past (open lease June flat $1,500 then July $1,200; total $2,700); T4 long lease closing Oct 12 → 5 invoices ($1,200/$1,500/$1,500/$1,500/$600 = $6,300, last final partial_end); T5 duplicate gate → PERIOD_OVERLAP (subprocess); T6 void invoice 2 + regenerate July → reproduces $350; T7 regenerate over SENT → PERIOD_OVERLAP + immutability (subprocess); T8 inverted dates → INVERTED_PERIOD (subprocess); T9 period_independent regression (legacy single invoice, audit columns NULL). Form auto-fill verified by deterministic node replication (fully-billed → Jun 7-Jul 7/31d; fresh → Jun 7-Jun 30/24d; 2nd segment → Jul 1-Jul 7/7d/final). **Existing corpus updated to R2 (behaviour change; The helper was split — `optimistic_lock_compare()` keeps the pure D73 timestamp normalization (still unit-tested), and `optimistic_lock_matches()` is now a flag gate: returns true (no conflict) whenever `FF_OPTIMISTIC_LOCKING` is off. NEW `config/app.php` constant `FF_OPTIMISTIC_LOCKING` (default false, env-overridable; defensive-default OFF if undefined). So all **29** editors (26 already on the helper + the 3 former raw-`!==` sites — `accounting/recurring/update.php`, `lib/Accounting/BudgetService.php`, `mileage_logs/update.php` — converted to the helper so the flag governs them too) stop emitting STALE_DATA in one place, with NO call-site churn and full reversibility (`FF_OPTIMISTIC_LOCKING=1` restores strict locking). **SCOPE — only optimistic locks:** business-rule 409s are untouched and intentionally preserved (they don't route through the helper): invoices/send.php precharge PRECHARGE_LOCKED/PRECHARGE_ALREADY_BILLED, invalid state transitions, immutable-record guards, etc. **Concurrent edits now resolve last-write-wins;** audit_log retains prior values where written (coverage varies by endpoint — e.g. units/update logs full old/new, compliance logs a notes string). When `$entityType === 'vehicle'` (default): all logic identical to before (OBD > GPS preference, D-B). | S-FORM-DRAFT-AUTOSAVE | 2026-06-16 | leases — reusable form-draft autosave helper (FF_FormDraft); applied to lease create + edit | **NEW reusable Alpine helper `window.FF_FormDraft` (public/assets/js/app.js, §07h) that prevents loss of in-progress edits on Back / refresh / accidental close.** Mirrors a form's reactive model to `localStorage` (debounced **500 ms**) under key `ff_draft:<formId>:<entityId>` with a payload of `{ v:<DRAFT_VERSION>, t:<epoch>, s:{ <section>:{ d, t } } }` — **versioned + timestamped + section-sliced**. On attach it offers a dismissible **restore banner** ("Unsaved changes from {relative time}" + Restore / Discard / ×, themed via app CSS vars so it's dark-mode safe, mounted as a sibling above the component root). **Features:** `exclude[]` (dot-path aware) field list never written to storage; **multi-page wizard support** — each page writes its own SECTION slice into the SAME entity key (merge, no clobber), final submit clears the whole key; optional `beforeUnloadWarn` (off by default); `pagehide`/`visibilitychange` **flush** so a Back/close mid-debounce never loses the last keystrokes; **idempotent `attach()`** (guards Alpine's double-`init()` from `x-init="init()"` + auto-`init` — caught live as a duplicate-banner bug and fixed). Picker ids excluded because FF_RecordPicker owns its own display state and can't be rehydrated at runtime. (b) `app/admin/leases/edit.php` `FF_EditLease()` — `attach({formId:'lease-edit',entityId:form.id,…, exclude:['id','updated_at']})`; `_draft.clear(true)` before the success redirect. **`updated_at` (optimistic-lock token, D19) is excluded so a restored draft can never re-inject a stale token** — restore only refills editable business fields, leaving the freshly server-rendered token intact. | S-CLOSE-OVERSHOOT | 2026-06-19 | fix — invoices billed PAST the lease's actual return date are never reconciled at close (prod: lease MTTS66 / INV-2026-00130 billed Jul 18→31 when the unit returned Jul 25) | **Root cause (diagnosed against prod): a lease that STARTS mid-month gets an activation `partial_start` Invoice 1 billed start_date → end-of-month (`date('Y-m-t')`). At activation `actual_return_date` is NULL so that is correct. When the lease is later CLOSED with an `actual_return_date` inside that same month, NOTHING shortened/credited the invoice — `legacy_handle_existing_full_month_draft()` only ever matched `billing_type='full_month'`, and the partial_end fallback was then suppressed by the S-FIX-2 Bug #6 coverage guard because month-end coverage already reached past the return. The "Jul 25" the operator sees is `actual_return_date`; `leases.end_date` was NULL. Confirmed across 7 prod invoices INV-2026-00126..00133 (minus 00132): leases MTTS62/63/64/65/66/67/69, every one returned inside its first partial_start month, all status=draft. MTTS67 (returned Oct, 3 months later) correctly got a partial_end — proving the close path only fails when the return lands inside the first partial_start month. **Fix (canonical, once-and-for-all):** new shared `api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php` (extracted the `adv_*` credit/void primitives + new `reconcile_overshoot_invoices()` + `lease_billable_extent()`), required by BOTH `close.php` and `bulk_close.php` so the two close paths cannot drift. On EVERY close, `reconcile_overshoot_invoices()` clamps each non-advance rental invoice whose `billing_period_end` > the lease's billable extent: draft straddle → void + regenerate shortened (engine-computed amount, Path-B self-correcting, OB untouched); sent/paid straddle → prorated credit note; wholly-past (incl. future-month full_month) → void/full credit. Extent = `lease_billable_extent()` = `actual_return_date` with the S-LEASE-RENTAL-DAY-TIME rule, matching `InvoiceGenerator` exactly so a shortened invoice's period_end agrees with its amount. full_month STRADDLE stays close.php's `legacy_handle` domain (preserves invoice_type=final + mileage append); bulk_close (no legacy_handle, no mileage) clamps it directly via the `$clampFullMonthStraddle` flag. Idempotent on reopen/reclose (strict `>` + a NOT-EXISTS adjustment-credit guard that blocks double-crediting sent invoices). Coverage anchor in close.php + bulk_close tail-guard now filter `billing_period_start <= extent` so a credited-but-immutable future invoice can't suppress the real tail. Advance reconciliation untouched (excluded by `generation_source<>'advance'`; T14 still 40/40). **5-agent adversarial review run; 2 confirmed findings deferred (see [[project_close_overshoot_fix]] + OPERATOR_FOLLOWUPS): sent/paid straddle credit is linear-day not tier-aware (pre-existing advance behavior); voiding a drawdown-carrying draft does not restore precharge_balance (narrow).** **Verified:** NEW `tests/_smoke_legacy_close_overshoot.php` 59/59 PASS (real activate-shape + real close/bulk_close/reopen HTTP endpoints; cases: draft straddle, sent straddle + credit, last-day no-clamp, time-of-day extent-1, reopen/reclose idempotency ×2, bulk_close clamp, future full_month void + real tail still billed, bulk full_month straddle). Regression: session4 advance 40/40, advance_close_mileage 6/6, billing_time_of_day 28/28, invoice_dating 28/28, bulk_close_tail 2/2, doc_freshness 29/29. **Data remediation (operator-run; prod is read-only for the agent):** `scripts/diagnose_close_overshoot.php` (read-only) + `scripts/remediate_close_overshoot_2026_06_19.php --apply --user-id=<id>` (idempotent; reuses `reconcile_overshoot_invoices`; all 7 prod invoices are drafts → void+regenerate, no OB impact). **Files:** NEW `api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php`, `tests/_smoke_legacy_close_overshoot.php`, `scripts/diagnose_close_overshoot.php`, `scripts/remediate_close_overshoot_2026_06_19.php`; CHANGED `api/v1/leases/close.php` (extract helpers + extent + reconcile call + coverage filter + extent-based partial_end + widened advance SELECT), `api/v1/leases/bulk_close.php` (require + clamp call + tail-guard filter + province join). **PROD posture:** code fix, no migration; operator runs the remediation script + an optional `ff-deploy`. | smoke 59/59 PASS (new); regression session4 40/40 + advance_close_mileage 6/6 + billing_time_of_day 28/28 + invoice_dating 28/28 + bulk_close_tail 2/2; doc_freshness 29/29 | decisions: ONE billable-extent definition (`lease_billable_extent`) shared by both close paths + scripts; close-time clamp is the canonical reconciliation point (generators can't know the future return); advance invoices stay the advance branch's domain; full_month straddle stays legacy_handle's domain in close.php (mileage/final) but is clamped in bulk_close. |

The `bcdiv(..., 2)` returns 2 decimal places which is the correct scale for km/miles in invoicing; if a future feature needs more precision (e.g. fuel-economy reports at 4 decimal places) it would call its own bcmath conversion. Three valid lease configurations are admitted: **(Model C)** `rate>0 + allowance>0` → bill only excess over period allowance; **(Model B Lite)** `rate>0 + allowance=0` → bill every km from km 0 (allowance=0 interpreted as "no included km", math: `excess = max(0, distance − 0) = distance`); **(Disabled)** `rate=0 + allowance=0 + precharge_enabled=0` → no mileage billing. The D-B HARD throw on `(allowance>0 + rate=0)` is preserved as a standalone guard (D133 unchanged semantics) since it can no longer be gated by `$mileageBillingExpected` post the rate-keying restructure. | D136 | Multi-agent discipline (locked 2026-05-07 via S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL; extended 2026-05-11 via S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE): only one write-mode Code Desktop session at a time should be active on `/Users/avi/Documents/fleetforge`. **Default mode:** single-agent serialization on main. Active session is registered in `FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md` with status `IN-FLIGHT` plus start timestamp, agent identifier (e.g. `desktop-1`, `desktop-2`), and the file/path domains expected to be touched. Every session start runs a pre-flight read of CURRENT_SESSIONS.md and halts for operator direction if any other session is marked IN-FLIGHT with overlapping file domains. **Read-only exemption:** audits, surveys, decision-surfacing, and any session that does not commit to main are exempt from serialization. They register as `IN-FLIGHT-RO` and may run concurrently with a write-mode session. Multiple IN-FLIGHT-RO sessions may also run concurrently. **Branch isolation fallback:** when the operator explicitly opts into parallel write work, agents use `session/<S-LABEL>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>` branches with the same D131 smoke gate per branch. Merge to main is operator-approved and includes a post-merge smoke run. Both branch SESSION LOG entries document the parallel split. **Author identity caveat:** git's author field is uniform across all Code Desktop agents. Reconstructing parallelism after the fact requires the SESSION LOG narrative + commit timestamps. **Registration commit requirement (locked 2026-05-11 via S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE):** IN-FLIGHT registration must be COMMITTED to main before any subsequent operation (file edit, DB write, branch creation). Working-tree-only registration does not count as registered. Pre-flight check Step 1.5 (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md `pre-flight check` section) verifies the registration is committed-clean before subsequent edits. **Enforcement:** relies on agent discipline reading CURRENT_SESSIONS.md, same model as D131 (smoke gates) and D127 (parity). No automated locking, no git hooks (MVP — defer until soft lock proves insufficient). (S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL; S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE) | Origin: K-6 (S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX C4, commits 764abf1 + ef050e7 same-session overlap) and S-ACCT-AUDIT (b74b947 mid-session injection, SESSION LOG entry backfilled in S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL commit) on 2026-05-07 are the canonical incidents that triggered this discipline; pre-K-6 history shows zero parallel events in 177 commits. **Registration commit requirement origin:** S-ACCT-FIX-A1 (2026-05-07) registered IN-FLIGHT in working tree, crashed without committing; downstream session S-DOC-STATUS-RECONCILE-CLOSE drafted under false premise that registration had reached main, requiring a post-merge S-DOC-STATUS-RECONCILE-CLOSE-FIXUP to remove the carryover IN-FLIGHT block. The branch isolation fallback addresses collision avoidance, not state-divergence avoidance — without the commit step, a session that registers IN-FLIGHT in working tree and crashes leaves the registration invisible to a fresh agent reading the file, and a downstream session can create a branch from working-tree carryover state. Backfilled here in S-DOCS-CLUSTER-2026-05-11 (D-D); the decision had already been locked in REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS via S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL (commit f195bee) but was not yet in this DECISIONS table — gap surfaced by S-D136-COMMIT-DISCIPLINE pre-work scan. | S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL (commit f195bee) locks the base discipline. K-12 (documentation divergence as bug class) locked in S-DOC-STATUS-RECONCILE-CLOSE applies — DECISIONS table absences are a discipline failure even when the canonical decision lives in REFERENCE.md. Future automated discipline gates (D-FRESHNESS smoke, if S-DOC-FRESHNESS-DISCIPLINE ships) should cross-check DECISIONS table membership against REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS to surface this class of gap mechanically. |

Browsers resolve those relative to the CSS file's URL. Placing the PNG files at `public/assets/vendor/leaflet/images/{marker-icon.png, marker-icon-2x.png, marker-shadow.png, layers.png, layers-2x.png}` — mirroring upstream's `leaflet/dist/images/` layout — means the default CSS works unmodified and no JS-side `L.Icon.Default.imagePath = '...'` override is needed. Cleaner upgrade path: re-fetching the upstream `dist/images/` set replaces these files in place; no consumer JS changes required. Alternative (JS imagePath override) was rejected because it adds a Leaflet-specific runtime hack to every map-rendering page and breaks if a future Leaflet version changes its image-loading model. | D188 | users.mfa_verified_until semantics (locked 2026-05-14 via S-AUTH-FIX D-A): NULL = MFA has never been blessed for this user via a remember-me cycle — re-prompt MFA on session restoration. NOT NULL = the datetime at which the MFA blessing expires. If NOW() < mfa_verified_until, auth_check_remember_me() skips the MFA challenge and restores the full session. If expired, the remember-me cycle still restores the session at password level (auth_login runs) but sets `$_SESSION['ff_mfa_pending']` so the next request is gated on MFA re-verification. Net effect: "Keep me signed in for 30 days" covers BOTH factors for 30 days from MFA completion, then transitions to a clean MFA re-prompt (not a full logout). Both are read off the same row by `auth_check_remember_me()`. Keeping them adjacent in the schema mirrors that pairing in the code and makes the relationship visible in DESCRIBE/dump output. A stolen remember_token alone is NOT sufficient to bypass MFA if mfa_verified_until has expired — the attacker would still hit the MFA wall on the next request. This closes the prior security gap where auth_check_remember_me() called auth_login() without checking MFA state, effectively granting MFA-verified status to any holder of a valid remember_token. | D-LESSOR-1-TERM | **Lease term for ASPE 3065 Criterion B is operator-supplied as a wizard input (`lease_term_months`), NOT derived from `leases.start_date`/`end_date`.** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-1 pre-flight AskUserQuestion. Rationale: `end_date` on a lease may represent the **intended return date** (often the customer's working estimate at contract signing, refined or shortened at close) rather than the **contractual term length** required by ASPE 3065.06(b) ("term ≥ 75% of economic life"). Deriving term from `TIMESTAMPDIFF(MONTH, start_date, end_date)` would silently overstate or understate Criterion B's ratio for any lease where the dates don't equal the contractual obligation. The wizard input pattern keeps the operator (who has the signed contract in hand) authoritative; it also avoids a phantom `term_months` column ambiguity (Trap 47). `LeaseClassificationService::evaluateCriterionB(int $leaseTermMonths, int $economicLifeMonths)` accepts the input directly. The classify.php endpoint validates `lease_term_months` as a required positive int (`clean_positive_int`). Applies to all future lessor-module sessions (LESSOR-2 amortization engine reads the same wizard input via `leases.economic_life_months` + the operator-confirmed term implicit in the schedule's row count). | Origin: S-ACCT-LESSOR-1 pre-flight 2026-05-19; AskUserQuestion offered 3 options (derive / wizard input / add a column). That combination cannot balance under double-entry: the receivable is booked at NET but the contra-account assumes it was booked at GROSS — the smoke's first-run output `DR=117,553.08 CR=189,554.08 diff=−72,001` (= the Unearned amount exactly) confirms the spec wording is internally inconsistent. **The bridge corrects this by using NET method consistently end-to-end.** Inception JE has 6 active lines (when all amounts > 0): `DR NI_current + DR NI_long_term + DR AccumDep + DR COGS / CR AssetCost + CR Sales Revenue` — Σ DR = initial_fair_value + accumulatedDep + COGS = initial_fair_value + (acquisition_cost − pv_unguaranteed) = Σ CR = acquisition_cost + (initial_fair_value − pv_unguaranteed). Period JE has 3 active lines (regular period) or 2 (BPO row, finance=0): `DR Cash (AR) / CR NI_current ($principal_reduction) + CR Finance Income ($finance_income)` — sums to $cash on each side by amortization-schedule construction (cash = principal + finance). Rationale for keeping the account: future ASPE disclosure reports (specifically Note 9 — Net Investment in Lease per §24.9) typically present a gross-vs-net reconciliation table that requires materializing the Unearned amount as a computed disclosure value; that computation can derive Unearned = Σ remaining cash_receipts + remaining unguaranteed residual − closing_net_investment at any point without needing a live GL contra balance. **Operator-locked alternative considered + rejected**: switching to GROSS method end-to-end would have required (a) redefining NI_current/NI_long_term split to use cash_receipt timing rather than principal_reduction, (b) changing the period JE to `CR NI = $cash_receipt` (not $principal) plus separate `DR Unearned / CR Finance Income` legs — invasive across activate.php / cron + tighter coupling to schedule shape. Per spec §24.5 ("Initial direct costs are deferred and amortized as a yield adjustment"), DF leases treat IDC fundamentally differently from sales-type leases: rather than hitting P&L immediately as Selling Expense, IDC is capitalized as a deferred asset that amortizes over the lease term as a contra to Finance Income recognition. This treatment reflects the economic reality that for DF leases (where FV = carrying, no selling profit), the lessor's "return" comes entirely from interest yield on the receivable; the IDC is a cost of generating that yield, so it should be matched against the yield as it's earned. **Implementation contrast**: sales-type IDC posts a SEPARATE JE (LSE-IDC-{contract}) at inception per D-LESSOR-3-IDC-TREATMENT; DF IDC is BUNDLED into the main inception JE as a DR line (no separate IDC JE for DF leases — onLeaseInception_DirectFinancing's response shape returns `idc_deferred` instead of `idc_je_id`). **Balance interaction**: the DF inception JE balances because `Σ DR = NI_current + NI_long_term + IDC + accumDep = initialNi + IDC + accumDep = (carrying − IDC) + IDC + accumDep = carrying + accumDep = acquisitionCost = Σ CR`. | D-LESSOR-4-IDC-AMORT-STRAIGHT-LINE | **DF IDC amortization is straight-line over the regular lease term: per-period amort = `initial_direct_costs / termMonths` (bcmath scale=2, truncating bcdiv).** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-4 session prompt directive. Three special cases that the implementation handles: (1) **Last regular period** (`period_number === termMonths`): the bcmath truncation accumulates rounding drift across periods 1..(termMonths−1). The last period absorbs the rounding tail via a DB lookup: `priorAmort = SUM(jel.credit) WHERE source_type='lease_period' AND source_id=lease AND account_id=deferred_idc_account_id` (over already-posted periods), then `thisAmort = initial_direct_costs − priorAmort`. This ensures `Σ amort = initial_direct_costs EXACTLY` to the penny, regardless of bcmath truncation in interior periods. Defensive: capped at 0 if priorAmort somehow exceeds total (would imply prior over-amortization — should never happen, but the guard avoids negative amort). (2) **BPO period** (`period_number > termMonths`, i.e. periodNumber === termMonths + 1 for leases with a BPO row): IDC amort = `$0.00`. The IDC asset is already fully amortized by the end of the regular term; the BPO row is a settlement event, not an amortization period. The JE for the BPO row therefore reverts to the standard 3-line shape (cash / NI / finance) — no Deferred IDC line. (3) **Interior periods** (any `1 ≤ period_number < termMonths`): straight-line slice `bcdiv($initialDirectCosts, (string) $termMonths, 2)`. **NOT effective-interest amortization** — explicitly straight-line per the spec wording and per common DF lease practice (CICA Handbook 3065.40 permits either method but straight-line is simpler and the difference vs effective-interest is immaterial for typical DF lease IDC amounts which are small relative to NI). **Defensive warn-only** when IDC amort > finance income for a period (smoke caught this on a particular schedule): produces negative `adjusted_finance`, which the JE renders as `DR Finance Income` (revenue reduction) rather than CR — mathematically valid and balanced, but unusual; logged via error_log for operator review. **Termination interaction**: when a DF lease terminates EARLY (before termMonths is reached), the un-amortized Deferred IDC balance remains on the books as a deferred asset; onLeaseTermination does NOT currently handle this case (residual IDC write-off at early termination is LESSOR-5 / LESSOR-6 scope when residual review workflows ship). For typical full-term DF leases this is a non-issue. | Origin: S-ACCT-LESSOR-4 session prompt 2026-05-19 (operator-pre-locked). | D-LESSOR-5-RECLASS-RATIO-METHOD | **NI reclass target derivation uses the schedule's TIMING (ratio of remaining principal in next 12 months vs beyond) applied to the on-books NI total — NOT the schedule's absolute principal sums.** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-5 mid-smoke bug catch. Formula: `currentRatio = bcdiv(scheduledNext12, scheduledTotal, 10)`; `target1090 = bcmul(currentTotal, currentRatio, 2)`; `target1600 = bcsub(currentTotal, target1090, 2)`. Where `scheduledNext12` = Σ principal_reduction on scheduled rows with period_date ≤ today+12mo, `scheduledTotal` = Σ principal_reduction on ALL scheduled rows, `currentTotal` = current1090 + current1600 from the GL trail (per D-LESSOR-5-NI-RECLASS-PER-LEASE). **Root cause of the abandoned absolute-sum approach**: under D-LESSOR-4-IDC-DEFERRAL, direct-financing leases have a structural divergence between schedule and on-books NI — the schedule is built from `FV − IDC` (LESSOR-2's `solveImplicitRate` uses `pvTarget = FV − IDC` for DF) but the inception JE posts NI = FV with IDC as a separate Deferred contra. So `Σ scheduled principal = FV − IDC` while `current1090 + current1600 = FV` — a structural gap of $IDC. Using schedule sums as targets directly would post a reclass that reduces total NI by $IDC each month, eroding the on-books receivable for no economic reason. **Smoke surfaced this**: S-ACCT-LESSOR-5 first DF smoke run showed `delta1090=$805.66 + delta1600=−$1,805.66 = −$1000.00` on a DF lease with IDC=$1,000.00 — the integrity invariant `delta1090 + delta1600 ≈ 0` (total NI unchanged by reclass) failed by exactly the IDC amount. **The ratio-based fix** sidesteps the structural gap entirely: the schedule's relative SPLIT between next-12mo and beyond is correct regardless of whether the absolute amounts match on-books NI; applying that proportion to the actual on-books NI total preserves both invariants — the time-based reclass split AND total-NI conservation. **Also handles**: (a) LESSOR-2's rounding-tail correction (D-LESSOR-4-PERIOD-PRINCIPAL-DERIVATION) which can cause schedule sums to drift by pennies from on-books NI — invisible to the ratio method. (b) Future residual impairments mid-lease — the impairment JE credits 1600, the schedule regen (D-LESSOR-5-PARTIAL-REGEN) rebuilds the lowered projection, and the ratio still correctly splits the (now-smaller) on-books NI total. **Sales-type leases** also use this method — they don't have the IDC structural gap (LESSOR-3 expenses IDC at inception), so for ST the schedule sums and on-books NI happen to match in normal operation and the ratio method gives identical results to the absolute-sum approach; the ratio is just universal. **bcmath scale=10** on the ratio division preserves penny-level precision when the final multiply happens at scale=2; smaller scales would accumulate visible drift on multi-year leases. | Origin: S-ACCT-LESSOR-5 mid-smoke algorithm bug 2026-05-19. Smoke output: `"NI reclass integrity drift for lease #2 (CN-441250-2026): delta1090=805.66 + delta1600=-1805.66 = 1000.00"` (where the lease had IDC=$1,000.00 exactly). Fix landed in closing commit `c774520`. | lib/Accounting/LeaseNiReclassService.php::computeBalancesForLease (the `$currentRatio = bcdiv(...)` block + the early-exit when scheduledTotal or currentTotal ≤ 0); D-LESSOR-4-IDC-DEFERRAL (the structural gap source for DF leases that motivates the ratio approach); D-LESSOR-5-NI-RECLASS-PER-LEASE (the JE-trail-based currentTotal source). |

| D-LESSOR-5-PARTIAL-REGEN | **`LeaseAmortizationService::regeneratePartial()` rebuilds the unposted (status='scheduled') portion of an amortization schedule WITHOUT touching posted history. Residual revision is a write-down event, not a re-pricing event.** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-5 session prompt directive. **Algorithm**: (1) Identify `lastPostedPeriod = MAX(period_number) WHERE status='posted'` (or 0 if none posted yet). `startFromPeriod = lastPostedPeriod + 1`. (3) **Apply residual-impairment adjustment to opening NI**: SUM the credits on the 1600 account from `lease_residual_impairment` JEs whose `entry_date >= MAX(entry_date) WHERE source_type='lease_period' AND status='posted'` — this captures any impairments posted AFTER the last period JE but BEFORE this regen call. Subtract that sum from openingNi. Keeps schedule's projection aligned with the post-impairment on-books NI. (4) DELETE all `status='scheduled'` rows. (5) Rebuild from `startFromPeriod` to `termMonths` using `LeaseAmortizationService::buildSchedule()`-style math at the LOCKED implicit_rate (not re-solved). (6) Apply same last-period rounding-tail correction as `buildSchedule()` (per D-LESSOR-4-PERIOD-PRINCIPAL-DERIVATION the schedule's stored principal stays as a UI projection; JEs derive from cash − finance). (7) Defensive flatten: if `openingNi` after impairment drops BELOW `guaranteed_residual_value` (the rounding target), set principal=0 + closing=opening on the last regular period rather than producing negative principal. (8) Append BPO row when present + within range. Re-solving the rate would constitute a different lease (a new "lease modification" event under §24.8 scope, not a residual revision). Future LESSOR-6 or LESSOR-7 sessions adding lease-modification workflow can introduce a separate rate-re-solve path; D-LESSOR-5-PARTIAL-REGEN stays scoped to residual write-downs only. **Idempotency**: regeneratePartial is NOT idempotent (re-calling deletes + rebuilds the scheduled rows again with the same inputs, producing the same output but writing a new audit_log row).
