| D-LESSOR-6-NO-REVERSAL | **Per ASPE 3063, once an impairment loss is recognized, it is NEVER reversed in subsequent periods — even if the asset's recoverable amount later increases.** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-6 session prompt directive. This is a key divergence from IFRS (IAS 36) which DOES permit impairment reversals up to the original carrying-amount-less-depreciation amount. ASPE's no-reversal stance is asymmetric (downward writedowns only, no upward recoveries) — same rationale as D-LESSOR-5-RESIDUAL-DOWNWARD-ONLY for unguaranteed residuals. **Implementation**: `ImpairmentTestService` has NO un-impair function — there is no API endpoint, no service method, and no admin UI affordance for reversing a posted impairment. Operators who post an impairment in error must use the existing JE reversal pathway (`JournalEntryService::reverse`) but that's an exceptional-case correction, not a normal-operations reversal. The reversal would also need a follow-up audit-trail note explaining it was an error correction, not an ASPE-compliant recovery. **Subsequent recoveries**: when an impaired asset's recoverable amount rises in a future year (e.g. used-truck market recovers), no reversing JE posts. Instead, the higher recoverable amount is reflected through normal depreciation on the lower NBV — the asset depreciates from its post-impairment carrying value over its remaining useful life. The lower NBV becomes the asset's permanent carrying-amount baseline. **Annual retest behavior**: a re-impaired asset (one that was impaired in a prior year and is impaired again in the current year for a further drop) DOES post an additional impairment JE; the no-reversal rule blocks UPWARD revisions, not subsequent DOWNWARD writedowns. UNIQUE(asset_id, fiscal_year, triggering_event) allows the same asset to have one 'annual' test row per year, capturing successive years' tests independently. | Origin: S-ACCT-LESSOR-6 session prompt 2026-05-19 (operator-pre-locked from ASPE 3063 — no-reversal is the canonical rule). | D-LESSOR-6-CF-ESTIMATOR | **Default undiscounted future cash flow estimator for ASPE 3063 step 1 (recoverability test): `avg_monthly_revenue × remaining_useful_months + estimated_disposal_value`.** Locked 2026-05-19 via S-ACCT-LESSOR-6 session prompt directive. **Formula components**: (a) `avg_monthly_revenue` = total unit revenue over the past N months (per `UnitProfitabilityService::getUnitRevenue` — same revenue rollup used by the Per-Unit P&L report per S-ACCT-UNIT) divided by the effective months in the window. Effective months = min(lookback_months, monthsSinceStart) so a brand-new asset with 3 months on the books doesn't get averaged over a 12-month window it didn't fully exist in. N is configurable via setting `accounting.impairment_cf_lookback_months` (default 12). (b) `remaining_useful_months` = max(0, useful_life_years × 12 − months_since_depreciation_start_date). Bounded at 0 floor so over-life assets don't get negative remaining months. (c) `estimated_disposal_value` defaults to `acc_fixed_assets.salvage_value` per setting `accounting.impairment_default_disposal_basis = 'salvage_value'`. Alternative bases `'manual'` (operator-supplied per-test) and `'market_lookup'` (reserved for future external valuation integration) are accepted by the setting schema but not yet wired into the estimator. **Operator override**: per-test `$cfOverride` parameter on `runTest()` / `runStep1()` bypasses the estimator entirely — operator supplies a specific undiscounted CF amount with their own basis (idle unit estimate, market-decline judgment, etc.). The override path stores `step_1_cf_source='operator_override'` in `acc_impairment_tests` so the test record carries the source-of-truth flag. **No-revenue-history case**: when the asset has no `equipment_unit_id` or the unit has zero invoice history in the lookback window, `avg_monthly_revenue` = 0 and the CF degrades to just `estimated_disposal_value`. Step 1 will almost certainly fail in that case (carrying > salvage) — correct behavior. Operator either provides an override or accepts the impairment. The breakdown_json captures `has_revenue_history=false` so the test detail page can surface that fact to the reviewer. **Why undiscounted**: ASPE 3063.20 specifies UNDISCOUNTED future cash flows for the step 1 recoverability test (contrast with step 2 fair-value measurement which IS at present value if discounting is appropriate). The estimator never applies a discount rate. **Why not declining-balance projection**: the formula assumes flat monthly revenue going forward — a simplification, but appropriate for fleet units where rental rates are typically stable over a unit's useful life with annual CPI adjustments. A more sophisticated estimator (declining utilization, ramp-down toward end of life) is operator-overridable per-asset via $cfOverride for the cases where it matters. | Origin: S-ACCT-LESSOR-6 session prompt 2026-05-19 (operator-pre-locked). Step 1 fail (carrying > CF) caught by Test 3. | lib/Accounting/ImpairmentTestService.php::estimateUndiscountedCf (the formula implementation with effective-months bounding + breakdown_json capture); db_migrations/202605191600_S-ACCT-LESSOR-6.sql (the 2 settings keys with defaults); lib/Accounting/UnitProfitabilityService.php::getUnitRevenue (the per-unit revenue rollup that feeds avg_monthly_revenue). |

No reasonable automated estimator exists for fleet equipment fair values; market data is fragmented and asset-specific. **UI workflow** (admin/accounting/impairment/index.php): two-pass interaction — (1) operator clicks "Run Annual Preview (Step 1)" → service returns per-asset verdicts with failing rows highlighted; (2) operator types FV + basis text into inline form for each failing asset; (3) operator clicks "Post Impairment JEs (N)" → service re-runs runAnnual with `fair_value_inputs` keyed by asset_id, completing step 2 + posting impairment JEs in a single batch. **fair_value_basis text field**: operator-provided rationale (e.g. "Ritchie Bros auction comp 2026-04", "NRV minus selling costs", "appraisal report from QualifiedCo dated 2026-04-15") stored as free text in `acc_impairment_tests.step_2_fair_value_basis` for the audit trail. Wrapping the SDK to inject these seams ends up the same size as a custom client. SDK saves OAuth dance + entity builders but adds a vendor dependency requiring override at every cross-cutting seam. Single-realm integration with very specific cross-cutting concerns favors custom. **Future revisit window: S-QBO-11 onward.** Consider pulling SDK entity facade classes (IPPInvoice, IPPCustomer with typed properties) as payload builders if hand-rolled associative-array payloads become unwieldy. | D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-2 | **`app/admin/oauth/qbo/callback.php` runs auth-context-free — no `require_auth()`, no `require_permission()`.** The OAuth state token IS the authentication proof per OAuth 2.0 authorization-code grant; the provider can only deliver the redirect to the registered `redirect_uri`, and only with a state we minted. Gating the callback on an active session is architecturally redundant AND practically broken under cross-origin redirects (K-22 Trap #59): during local dev under ngrok the callback arrives on the ngrok origin while the session was established on `fleetforge.test`, so the session cookie is not sent and `$_SESSION` is empty at callback time — `require_auth()` redirects to the login page and the OAuth code is lost. The same class of failure applies to any future cross-origin redirect path Intuit (or another provider) may introduce. `init.php` retains `require_auth() + require_permission('quickbooks', 'edit_credentials')` because init is operator-initiated (button click in Settings), not provider-initiated. The audit attribution that `require_auth` would have provided is preserved via D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-4 (initiated_by_user_id captured at init time, recovered at callback time from `acc_oauth_states`). Locked 2026-05-20 via S-QBO-OAUTH-FIX. | Origin: K-22 Trap #59 surfaced during S-QBO-1 sandbox OAuth setup 2026-05-20; the architectural fix was queued as S-QBO-OAUTH-FIX in D-S-QBO-1-OAUTH-DOCS-LOCK and shipped this session. Companions: K-22 Trap #59 in REFERENCE.md §11 (the architectural cause), D-S-QBO-1-CALLBACK-HOTFIX (the prior hotfix that re-instated `require_auth` after a temporary bypass — this decision now permanently removes it for the right architectural reason), D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-4 (how audit attribution is preserved without session). | `app/admin/oauth/qbo/callback.php` (the file with no `require_auth`/`require_permission` calls); `lib/OAuth/StateManager.php::verifyAndConsume` (the atomic auth proof); `tests/_smoke_oauth_state.php` C9 (structural assertion that callback.php has no `require_auth\(`/`require_permission\(` lines); FLEETFORGE_QUICKBOOKS_SPEC.md §5.1.1 (the "Why the callback is auth-context-free" subsection). |
| D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-3 | **OAuth state token lifecycle: 600s (10-min) TTL + single-use enforcement + 24h forensic cleanup buffer.** Each generated state token persists to `acc_oauth_states` with `expires_at = DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL 600 SECOND)` (D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-3a — 10 minutes is generous for slow Intuit MFA + slow-tab flows but narrows the leak window). Consumption is atomic via `UPDATE … SET used_at = NOW() WHERE state_token=? AND provider=? AND expires_at>NOW() AND used_at IS NULL` — single-use enforced by the `used_at IS NULL` predicate + `affected_rows` race detection (D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-3b — no FOR UPDATE row lock needed; if `affected_rows = 0` either the row doesn't exist, is expired, has been used, or is for a different provider — all treated identically as "invalid" without differentiating to avoid leaking info to a probing attacker). Cleanup is opportunistic via `StateManager::generate()` running `DELETE FROM acc_oauth_states WHERE expires_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR` on every call (D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-3c — no dedicated cron; the 24h forensic buffer keeps recent expired/abandoned rows for audit ("operator X attempted to connect at 14:32 but never came back — was that them?")). **K-22 silent catch during smoke build**: the original implementation used PHP `date('Y-m-d H:i:s', time()+$ttl)` for `expires_at` which formats in php.ini timezone (Herd default America/Chicago = UTC-6) while MySQL `NOW()` runs in UTC — the 6h offset put `expires_at` in the past relative to MySQL's clock and rejected every fresh token. Fixed by switching to raw INSERT with `DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL ? SECOND)` so both clocks live MySQL-side. Worth a K-22 catalog entry (#60) at the next docs-lock pass. Locked 2026-05-20 via S-QBO-OAUTH-FIX. | Origin: S-QBO-OAUTH-FIX prompt 2026-05-20 specified the TTL, single-use semantics, and 24h buffer; smoke build surfaced the timezone bug live and the fix is now baked into StateManager. Companions: K-22 Trap #59 (the cross-origin session failure this entire mechanism addresses), D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-2 (the architectural reason single-use enforcement matters — the callback can't fall back to session-based deduplication). | `lib/OAuth/StateManager.php::generate` (raw INSERT with `DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL ? SECOND)` — NOT db_insert with PHP-side date()); `lib/OAuth/StateManager.php::verifyAndConsume` (atomic UPDATE-with-condition); `lib/OAuth/StateManager.php::cleanup` (manual cleanup helper); `acc_oauth_states.expires_at` + `acc_oauth_states.used_at` (the columns enforcing the TTL + single-use predicates); `tests/_smoke_oauth_state.php` C4/C5/C8 (single-use + expiry + cleanup assertions). |
| D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-4 | **Audit attribution for OAuth callbacks preserved via `acc_oauth_states.initiated_by_user_id` captured at init time, recovered at consume time, looked up to `users.name` via `ff_qbo_lookup_user_name()` helper.** `init.php` calls `StateManager::generate('quickbooks', 600, current_user_id(), $remoteIp)` while still under `require_auth()`, capturing the operator's id at the moment they clicked "Connect" + the initiating IP for forensics. `callback.php` (auth-context-free per D-QBO-OAUTH-FIX-2) calls `StateManager::verifyAndConsume($token, 'quickbooks', $remoteIp)` which returns `['initiated_by_user_id' => ?int, 'initiated_at' => string]`; the user_id is used as `user_id` on both `audit_log` INSERTs (success path `action='create'` + failure path `action='update'`), and `ff_qbo_lookup_user_name($id)` resolves to the display name (returns `'system'` if id is null or if the user was deleted since init — keeps audit inserts intact rather than failing on a NOT NULL `user_name` column). The FK `acc_oauth_states.initiated_by_user_id → users.id ON DELETE SET NULL` ensures user deletion doesn't break the OAuth flow's persistence layer. **Why not pass user_id through the OAuth round-trip via Intuit?** The state parameter is the only round-trip channel and is reserved for CSRF/auth proof; coupling user identity to it would conflate two concerns. The acc_oauth_states row is the right persistence boundary — it lives only as long as the OAuth flow needs it. | D-QBO-5-2 | **Customer auto-match algorithm: normalize → exact name → Levenshtein ≤ 3 → email → phone last-7-digits → unmatched.** Each FF customer is compared against the QBO customer list in this cascade order; first hit wins. Pass details: **(1) Normalization** lowercases, strips punctuation (.,;:'"`-_), removes whole-word corporate suffixes (inc / incorporated / ltd / limited / llc / corp / corporation / co — optionally followed by a period), collapses whitespace → "Acme Corp Ltd." / "Acme Inc" / "ACME, LLC" all normalize to "acme". **(2) Levenshtein ≤ 3** runs only if at least one side's normalized name is ≥ 5 chars (avoids trivial-distance false positives on short names — 3 edits can turn any short name into any other). Confidence='high'. **(3) Email** case-insensitive exact match on both sides non-empty. Confidence='medium'. **(4) Phone last-7-digits** strips all non-digits then compares the last 7 (handles +1 country code variations vs. plain 10-digit). Confidence='low'. **(5) Unmatched** returns null → row stays as ff_only (FF side) or qbo_only (QBO side). **Operator override is final**: any row with match_confidence='manual' is preserved by auto_match.php and never overwritten by subsequent auto-match runs (the endpoint reads manual-locked FF ids up front + skips them in the decisions loop). The cascade order reflects false-positive risk — exact name is the lowest-risk signal, phone match is the highest-risk (shared phones across related entities). Locked 2026-05-20 via S-QBO-5. | Origin: S-QBO-5 prompt 2026-05-20 specified the cascade order + corporate-suffix normalization list. | D-QBO-5-FIX-1-1 | **QBO `QueryResponse` 1-row-object → array normalization implemented at `QuickBooksClient::query()` boundary, NOT per-Pusher.** Intuit's REST API serializes entity collections under `QueryResponse.<EntityType>` as: missing (0 rows), bare object (1 row), or array of objects (N>1 rows). The asymmetric 1-row case was originally handled with a defensive wrap inside `CustomerPuller::pullAll()` (S-QBO-5 ship). Recognized post-ship as a pattern that would replicate across every future Pusher (Vendor / Invoice / Payment / Bill / JournalEntry / etc.) — 10+ places of the same defensive code. Option A would have left the per-Pusher wraps in place and accepted the repetition; Option B (locked here) centralizes the normalization at the single HTTP boundary. `query()` now post-processes its `dispatch()` return: walks every uppercase-keyed field under `QueryResponse` and wraps bare-object values into single-element arrays. Camelcase metadata (`startPosition`, `maxResults`, `totalCount`) and the envelope itself are passed through untouched, preserving pagination for `CustomerPuller`'s `STARTPOSITION` loop. The coercion is exposed as `QuickBooksClient::normalizeQueryResponse(array $response): array` (public static) so offline smokes can exercise it without mocking the cURL/auth/retry stack — matches the existing `_testClassify` accessor pattern. Locked 2026-05-21 via S-QBO-5-FIX-1. | Origin: S-QBO-5 live sandbox verification surfaced the per-Pusher defensive wrap; operator recognized the pattern would replicate across S-QBO-6/7/11/13/16/17/18/19/21 Pusher sessions and made the architectural call to centralize. Companion: K-22 Trap #60 (the catalog entry that documents the underlying Intuit API quirk for future Pusher authors). | `lib/QuickBooksClient.php::query` + `lib/QuickBooksClient.php::normalizeQueryResponse` (the implementation); `tests/_smoke_qbo_client.php` C7 (offline coverage); future S-QBO-6/7/11/13/16/17/18/19/21 Pusher sessions (they consume the normalized response without per-call defensive wraps). |

The first push for that entity has to be a POST not a PUT — QBO's update endpoint requires a valid Id + SyncToken pair. Return status `'created_from_update'` (NOT plain `'created'`) so the worker's audit log distinguishes the demoted case from a clean operator-driven create — useful for forensic reconstruction of how a customer's sync state evolved. Triggers when a mapping was created by S-QBO-5's auto-match flow (ff_only state) without ever being pushed, or when the operator manually linked a brand-new FF customer to an arbitrary qbo_id string via the UI without pulling first. The S-QBO-6 CustomerPusher implements this in `pushImpl()` via `if ($operation === 'update' && ($mapping === null || empty($mapping['qbo_customer_id']))) { $effectiveOperation = 'create'; }`. Extension to D-QBO-6-2 (the create-side idempotency check); together they make pushCreate idempotent in both directions — create when nothing exists, no-op when already mapped. FF recomputes and compares via `hash_equals()` (constant-time — protects against timing-based signature-guessing attacks; NEVER use === for HMAC compares). QboWebhookSignature::verify() returns false in that case so no webhook can be accepted until operator configures the token. Same fail-closed rule applies to empty received_signature (missing header). When account B (the other side) is also mapped, the next pull cycle for B will pick up Transfer:N from B's perspective (positive amount → deposit) — same composite key qbo_bank_txn_id="Transfer:N" but DIFFERENT (ff_bank_account_id, signed amount). FF acc_bank_transactions has no native from/to twin-row concept; the per-side independent INSERT mirrors how operators see bank statements (each account statement shows its side only). Note: the UNIQUE constraint is on qbo_bank_txn_id alone, so the second-side INSERT updates the first map row rather than creating a sibling; this is acceptable v1 behavior (operator sees one mirror row; the other side is implicit). A follow-up could enhance to track both sides via composite (qbo_bank_txn_id, ff_bank_account_id) UNIQUE — deferred. Locked 2026-05-29 via S-QBO-20. | Origin: spec §8.12 pseudocode emits one query per mapped-account perspective; per-account independence matches bank statement semantics. Companion: future enhancement to track both Transfer sides via composite UNIQUE. | `lib/QboPushers/BankTransactionPuller.php::rowMatchesAccount` (Transfer From OR To match); `::extractEconomicData` Transfer branch (signed amount derived per side); `tests/_smoke_qbo_bank_cdc.php` C9 (Transfer upsert from one side). |

| D-QBO-15-5 | **Idempotency: existing pending+unexpired initiation row returns the SAME URL on subsequent `PaymentInitiator::generate` calls; existing expired+pending row gets marked 'expired' + new URL generated.** When portal customer clicks "Pay Online" twice within the URL TTL (default 30 min per `quickbooks.payments.url_ttl_minutes` setting), the second call MUST NOT generate a new Intuit Payments URL — that would create a second pending initiation row + leave the first orphan + cost an extra Intuit API call. Instead: `generate()` looks up the latest pending row for the invoice; if status='pending' AND expires_at > NOW(), return the same URL + token + expires_at. If status='pending' AND expires_at <= NOW() (TTL exceeded), atomically UPDATE that row to status='expired' (cleanup) + proceed to new URL generation. This guarantees the D-QBO-15-1 single-pending-per-invoice invariant is preserved even under high-frequency duplicate clicks. | D-GUARD-1 | Schema integrity invariant — migrations ⊆ master | `tests/_smoke_migrations_reproduce_master.php` asserts every table/column a `db_migrations/` delta introduces is reflected in `FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql` (net of create-then-drop). **STATIC parse, NOT a from-zero `migrate` build** — `db_migrations/` holds incremental deltas: 112 of master's 153 tables are created by no migration (base schema lives only in master), and 40/90 migrations are non-idempotent (re-apply onto master errors), so from-zero reproduces 46 tables and dynamic replay false-fails. This is the missing companion to D127 (master-vs-live): D127 proves master==live, D-GUARD-1 proves master==migrations. The 2026-06-05 outage lived in that gap. Forensic `*_backup_S_MILEAGE_*` tables ARE kept in master so they verify normally — no carve-out that could hide drift. (Originally specced as "from-zero reproduces master exactly"; redefined to the feasible subset relation, operator-approved via AskUserQuestion after the architecture was empirically established.) | The prod-500 root cause was master silently lagging a migration; a from-zero build is impossible given the delta-only migration model, so the static subset relation is the strongest feasible, hermetic enforcement. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1. |
| D-GUARD-2 | `db_migrations/` is the ONLY place schema SQL may live — ABSOLUTE | `tests/_smoke_no_stray_schema_sql.php` (the PRIMARY net) fails the gate if (i) `database/migrations/` exists, or (ii) any `*.sql` containing CREATE/ALTER TABLE sits anywhere outside `db_migrations/` + `FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql`. **No whitelist, no exception path** — a tolerated "archive" location would reopen the exact crack that caused the outage. Pure data seeds (INSERT-only) are allowed. Deprecated historical SQL is kept on-disk neutered to `*.sql.txt` (`scripts/archive/legacy_database_migrations/`). | Today's bug was a CREATE TABLE filed in the unscanned `database/migrations/` dir; `migrate --apply` (which scans only `db_migrations/`) never carried it to prod. Forcing every schema change to be a scanned delta makes that structurally impossible. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1. |
| D-GUARD-3 | Nothing schema-bearing lost when closing the deprecated dir | Before the deprecated `database/migrations/` dir was retired, every migration that existed only there was already reconciled into `db_migrations/` (`b845bb6` moved 027–038; `dd500ec` added `role_permission_overrides` to `db_migrations/` + master) — so the from-migrations build reproduces every table. S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1 verified this NOT by trust but by the green keystone (D-GUARD-1): every `db_migrations/` table is reflected in master, and the neutered `*.sql.txt` archive copies are independently re-proven non-essential. The deprecated dir's deletion predates this session (C2 was a no-op contraction per D130). | Closing a migration dir must never silently drop a table; the keystone is the machine-checked proof, replacing any human "trust me it's reconciled". Locked 2026-06-05 via S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1. |

A permission-CONFIG read going down must degrade gracefully, not take down all auth. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-AUTH-FAILOPEN-1. |
| D-FAILOPEN-2 | Fail-open scope = ONLY the override loaders; identity reads stay fail-CLOSED | The try/catch is surgical — only the two override/config loaders in the session-bootstrap path. NO global `db_select` wrapper. Auth-IDENTITY reads (remember-me token validation, the `users` lookup) keep failing CLOSED (a failure there → unauthenticated, never silently authenticated). Mirrors `Mailer::isEmailDisabled()`'s targeted fail-open. | Fail-open is correct for permission CONFIG (absence = use defaults) but catastrophic for identity (absence must never grant access). Verified by `tests/_smoke_auth_failopen.php` SC5 (subprocess stderr carries both lines). | A graceful degradation that hides the underlying breakage just converts a loud outage into a silent, lingering security/availability regression. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-AUTH-FAILOPEN-1. |
| D-DEPLOY-1 | Single atomic, gated, abort-on-failure `bin/deploy.sh` | `set -euo pipefail` + explicit `abort` on every step — never continues past a failed pull/backup/migrate/health. 10 ordered steps: clean-tree precheck (tracked-only) → fetch → show-incoming + y/N confirm (`--yes` to skip) → pull --ff-only → DB backup (pre-migrate rollback point) → composer install → migrate --apply → assert 0 pending → reload php-fpm → health gate (200 + db + 0 pending + critical tables + login 200 + no fresh fatals) → deploy-log. ADDITIVE hardening of the pre-existing script (preserves composer + the 2026-05-20 "always-run-all-steps, never skip migrate/reload" lock + its incident comments). The y/N confirm gates WHICH COMMITS SHIP, not WHICH STEPS RUN — orthogonal to, and reconciled with, the 2026-05-20 no-step-skipping rule. | Today's outage reached prod because the ad-hoc deploy had no gate to catch a schema lag before serving traffic. One command that aborts on any failure removes the human-error surface. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1. |
| D-DEPLOY-2 | `health.php` reports migrate-state + critical-table presence; `pending>0` = UNHEALTHY | `api/v1/health.php` exposes `migrations{pending,ok}` + `schema{ok}` publicly (counts/booleans, not sensitive — the deploy gate curls unauthenticated) + authed-only `schema.missing[]`. `pending>0` OR a missing critical table (users, user_roles, role_permission_overrides, user_permission_overrides, settings, schema_migrations, customers, leases, invoices) → `status:degraded`. Computed via a light `listFiles ∖ listApplied` Runner path (no per-file sha256, no mysql-binary shell-out); each sub-check try/catch'd so it degrades, never 500s the health endpoint. Paired CLI gate: `bin/migrate.php --assert-applied` (exit 4 on pending/drift; `--status` left exit-0 per its contract). | Makes a schema lag a one-curl check any monitor or the deploy gates on — turning the invisible failure mode that caused the 2026-06-05 outage into an explicit, observable signal. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1. |
| D-DEPLOY-3 | Paths/services parameterized; `--dry-run` mode | Every path/URL/service name in `bin/deploy.sh` is `FF_DEPLOY_*` env-overridable so the SAME script serves staging and prod. `--dry-run` prints the full ordered sequence and executes nothing destructive (no root required) — the only safe dev-side preview of a script that cannot be e2e-tested off-prod. | A deploy script that only works on one host can't be rehearsed on staging; staging rehearsal is exactly the 2026-05-20 lesson. Dry-run lets operators read the plan before committing. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1. |
| D-DEPLOY-4 | Rollback documented in `docs/runbooks/deploy.md` | Rollback = revert code to the prior HEAD (printed by deploy.sh + recorded in `logs/deploy.log`) + reload php-fpm. Additive migrations (new table / nullable column) need only the code revert — the reverted code ignores the extra schema. DESTRUCTIVE migrations (drop/rename/transform) restore the step-5 pre-deploy dump via `scripts/restore_db.php` per `restore_drill.md`. After any rollback, re-run the health gate and require `status:ok` + `pending:0`. | A deploy you can't reverse is a deploy you can't safely run. The pre-deploy backup (step 5) exists precisely to be the rollback point. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1. |
| D-CLASS4-1 | CLASS 4 (doc_freshness) counts ALL write-mode IN-FLIGHT blocks globally; ≥2 write entries pass only if all carry `D136-CONCURRENT: approved` (locked 2026-06-05 via S-CLASS4-COUNTER-FIX) | `tests/_smoke_doc_freshness.php` CLASS 4 block-extraction was a single `preg_match()` — it captured ONLY the FIRST `### IN-FLIGHT` block. A second session registered in a separate `### IN-FLIGHT` block (after `---`) was invisible, so 2 stacked write-sessions never tripped the ≤1 rule (observed live in S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1 pre-flight). **Fix:** `preg_match_all()` collects ALL `### IN-FLIGHT` blocks; per-entry split on `**S-LABEL** — ` boundaries checks each entry's metadata. **Policy:** ≤1 write-mode IN-FLIGHT → GREEN; ≥2 write entries all carrying `D136-CONCURRENT: approved` in their metadata block → GREEN (annotated disjoint concurrency); ≥2 with any bare (unannotated) entry → RED. | S-AUTH-FAILOPEN-1 + S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1 + S-DEPLOY-SAFETY-1 all ran as operator-approved concurrent write sessions, but the gate was not enforcing. The fix restores the D136 one-write-slot guarantee while preserving the approved-concurrent workflow via the structured annotation. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-CLASS4-COUNTER-FIX. |
| D-CLASS4-2 | `D136-CONCURRENT: approved` is the structured annotation for operator-approved concurrent writes; free prose in SESSION LOG does not count (locked 2026-06-05 via S-CLASS4-COUNTER-FIX) | When the operator authorizes two or more write sessions to run concurrently (disjoint domains, specific-path `git add`), EACH concurrent write entry in its `### IN-FLIGHT` metadata block must carry `D136-CONCURRENT: approved` (case-insensitive, on its own line in the metadata, before the next `**S-LABEL**` boundary). The annotation must appear AT REGISTRATION TIME (committed to main per the D136 registration commit requirement). Free-prose notes in the SESSION LOG narrative (e.g. "ran alongside S-X") are historical record only — they are written AFTER the session ships and are not visible to the CLASS 4 check during the session. Format (each concurrent IN-FLIGHT entry): `  D136-CONCURRENT: approved`. **D-CLASS4-2 verified (5 cases):** 0 IN-FLIGHT → GREEN; 1 bare → GREEN; 2 bare separate blocks → RED (S-SESSION-A, S-SESSION-B); 2 both-annotated → GREEN; 2 one-annotated/one-bare → RED (S-SESSION-B missing). | The existing convention (free prose in SESSION LOG) was not parseable at check time — CLASS 4 ran AFTER the session shipped so the narrative wasn't in the IN-FLIGHT block during enforcement. A minimal structured token parsed at check time restores enforcement without blocking the approved-concurrent workflow. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-CLASS4-COUNTER-FIX. |
| D-SAMSARA-DELETE-1 | FleetForge unit delete is one-directional — it does NOT propagate to Samsara (locked 2026-06-05 via S-SAMSARA-DELETE-DECOUPLE) | Neither `api/v1/equipment/units/delete.php` (single soft-delete) nor `api/v1/equipment/units/bulk_delete.php` (bulk soft-delete) may call `SamsaraClient::deleteTrailer()`. Dropping a unit in FF — e.g. a trailer we don't want to import/track — must leave the real Samsara asset untouched, so FF housekeeping can never destroy live fleet data. Intentional decoupling has a dedicated path: `api/v1/samsara/unlink.php`, which NULLs the FF↔Samsara link without deleting either record. The create-time auto-link (`create.php`) and update-time sync (`update.php`) are RETAINED — only the delete write-back is removed. `SamsaraClient::deleteTrailer()` is left in place (zero callers) rather than deleted, to keep this session's blast radius to the two delete endpoints. Originated as SAMSARA-3, which had wired delete→Samsara-delete into both paths; operator reversed the policy because a one-way delete is the safe default for fleet data we don't own the lifecycle of. | A FF-side delete is a local bookkeeping action; it should never reach out and destroy an external system-of-record asset. Making delete one-directional removes a data-loss footgun while preserving the explicit, named decouple path for the rare case where severing the link IS the intent. Locked 2026-06-05 via S-SAMSARA-DELETE-DECOUPLE. |
| D-BASELINE-1 | `000_baseline.sql` captures full current base schema; fresh DB from migrations == master (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | `db_migrations/000_baseline.sql` is a full-schema snapshot (all 156 tables, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) that makes "fresh DB built entirely from migrations equals master" true and mechanically enforced. Before this baseline, 113 of 156 master tables had no corresponding migration — a from-zero build reproduced only 43 tables and the D-GUARD-1 static keystone couldn't detect "a table edited into master with no delta." The baseline is a fixed 2026-06-06 snapshot (D-BASELINE-6); it is NEVER updated for new schema changes. | The 2026-06-05 outage class was partially closed by S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1 (static migrations⊆master), but the residual sub-case — a table edited directly into master with no `db_migrations/` delta — could only be closed by a full-schema baseline that makes from-zero == master dynamically verifiable. Hermetically proven: SC1 diff is CLEAN; SC2 phantom table causes keystone RED. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BASELINE-2 | Pre-baseline deltas superseded and archived to `.sql.txt` (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | All 96 `db_migrations/*.sql` files that predate `000_baseline.sql` are renamed to `.sql.txt`. `Runner.listFiles()` only reads `*.sql`, so they are permanently skipped in migration plans. `Runner.verify()` treats a `.sql.txt` sibling as "archived ok" (keyed off file existence, NOT checksum — existing prod holds REAL checksums for those 96 rows from when they were originally applied, not the empty ones a fresh build seeds). History is preserved on disk; the files are not deleted. | Archiving to `.sql.txt` is the established neutering pattern in this repo (16 `scripts/archive/legacy_database_migrations/*.sql.txt` from S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1). It satisfies D-GUARD-2 (no stray schema SQL — `.sql.txt` files are not parsed) while preserving audit history. The `.sql.txt` approach was the only option that satisfied all three constraints simultaneously: (1) Runner skips the files, (2) existing prod `schema_migrations` rows for those files pass `--verify`, and (3) D-GUARD-2 doesn't flag them. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BASELINE-3 | `000_baseline` NEVER runs destructively on an existing DB — pre-marked applied WITHOUT running on existing prod (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | `000_baseline.sql` is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `INSERT IGNORE` only — a mathematical no-op on any DB that already has the full schema (SC3/SC4 hermetically verified). However, to prevent it from even being attempted via `migrate --apply` on an existing prod DB, `bin/deploy.sh` step 7 checks that `000_baseline.sql` is already recorded in `schema_migrations` BEFORE running `migrate --apply`. If not pre-marked, the deploy aborts with a `baseline_reconcile.md` reference. The one-time manual reconcile procedure is documented in `docs/runbooks/baseline_reconcile.md`: INSERT the pre-mark row → verify (`--status` expects N+1 applied, 0 pending) → run `migrate --apply` (no-op) → reload → health gate. | The deploy.sh guard transforms a "safe no-op if it runs" into a "never runs via normal path on existing prod." Belt-and-suspenders: even if the guard were bypassed, the file is still a guaranteed no-op. The guard exists because the reconcile runbook must be executed as a conscious deliberate operator step (especially given prod's current frozen state and pending catch-up), not automatically by the deploy script. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BASELINE-4 | D-GUARD-1 keystone upgraded to genuine from-zero rebuild (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | `tests/_smoke_migrations_reproduce_master.php` rewritten from a STATIC parse (migrations⊆master subset relation) to a GENUINE from-zero rebuild: SC1 — create `fleetforge_baseline_fresh_test` scratch DB → apply all `db_migrations/*.sql` sorted → dump → normalize → diff vs master-loaded-scratch → must be 0 lines (CLEAN). SC2 (negative test) — append phantom `CREATE TABLE _sc2_phantom_table_guard_test` to normalized master COPY (temp file; real master untouched) → diff vs from-zero dump → must be NON-EMPTY (keystone catches tables-in-master-with-no-delta). SC3/SC4 — create `fleetforge_baseline_prod_sim_test` → load master.sql → apply 000_baseline.sql → dump → diff vs master → CLEAN + 0 errors (proves the baseline is a genuine no-op on a full-schema DB). The prior static-parse check is superseded because the `000_baseline` migration is what makes the from-zero invariant achievable in the first place. | The static subset check (S-SCHEMA-GUARD-1) was the strongest feasible enforcement BEFORE the baseline existed. Once 000_baseline is present, the DYNAMIC check (actual DB build + diff) becomes achievable and is strictly stronger: it catches not only "table introduced by migration but absent from master" (the original outage class) but also "table edited into master with no delta at all" (the residual gap). SC2 is the machine-checked proof that the keystone bites in both directions. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BASELINE-5 | DO NOT touch prod; all baseline validation is hermetic (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | All SC1–SC4 validation runs against scratch DBs (`fleetforge_baseline_fresh_test`, `fleetforge_baseline_prod_sim_test`) that are created and dropped by the smoke test. The dev DB is never destructively mutated. Prod is never touched. The prod reconcile is a SEPARATE documented operator step (`docs/runbooks/baseline_reconcile.md`) to be executed when prod is fully caught-up to main — it is NOT part of this session. The pre-condition for running the reconcile runbook is: prod must already hold the COMPLETE current schema before the baseline is introduced (never combine "catch prod up" and "introduce baseline" in one motion). | Prod's current state is frozen and behind main, missing post-freeze deltas including the CCA tables. Touching it during this session would be destructive and premature. The runbook documents the safe one-time procedure in full; executing it is an operator responsibility. Hermetic validation means the session's stop conditions are verifiable and green without ever touching the production DB. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BASELINE-6 | Go-forward rule: new schema changes are new delta files + update master; 000_baseline is a fixed snapshot (locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE) | After the baseline reconcile runs on prod, normal deployments resume via `bin/deploy.sh`. For all future schema changes: (1) write a new delta migration `db_migrations/YYYYMMDDHHII_label.sql`; (2) update `FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql` to reflect the change; (3) run `bash scripts/precommit_doc_check.sh` — the upgraded D-GUARD-1 keystone enforces from-zero == master; (4) commit both files together. `000_baseline.sql` is a fixed 2026-06-06 snapshot and is NEVER edited or updated for new schema changes. The `INSERT IGNORE` seed block inside it (the 96 pre-baseline rows) is also never modified — it only seeds a fresh-DB bootstrap; on existing DBs those rows are already present and the INSERT IGNORE no-ops. | Editing the baseline for new schema changes would break the immutability invariant (checksums would drift for existing-prod rows, and the diff-vs-master test would fail for anybody who had already applied it). The delta-file model is the correct go-forward approach; the baseline is a foundation, not a living document. Documented in `docs/runbooks/baseline_reconcile.md` §Go-forward workflow. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-SCHEMA-BASELINE. |
| D-BACKUP-1 | Dropbox connects via one-time OAuth; offline refresh token stored encrypted in settings (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1) | The Dropbox API supports offline access via an OAuth 2.0 refresh token that never expires until explicitly revoked. The S-BACKUP-1 session seeds `dropbox.app_key`, `dropbox.app_secret` (is_sensitive=1), and `dropbox.refresh_token` (is_sensitive=1) in the settings table. The OAuth flow itself (authorization redirect → callback → token exchange → store) is implemented in S-BACKUP-2. The `connected_account` key stores the Dropbox account display name populated at the callback. This design avoids requiring credentials on every run (no username/password polling) and survives server restarts without user re-auth. | Refresh-token storage is the industry-standard pattern for background/cron OAuth clients. Alternatives considered: (a) short-lived access tokens (rejected: require per-run re-auth or hourly refresh cron); (b) service accounts (not supported by the Dropbox API — apps connect to a user's account). The is_sensitive=1 flag ensures app_secret and refresh_token are masked in UI and redacted from audit logs. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1. |
| D-BACKUP-2 | Dropbox backup cadence: DB daily + uploads weekly (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1) | The existing S3 backup crons run DB every 6 hours and uploads every Sunday. For Dropbox (implemented in S-BACKUP-2+), the cadence is reduced: DB backup daily (one per day at 00:00 UTC) and storage tarball weekly (Sunday, same as S3). Rationale: Dropbox is a secondary off-site copy for disaster-recovery; the tight 6-hour S3 cadence is for operational recovery where the latest backup is critical. A daily Dropbox DB copy satisfies the off-site requirement without burning Dropbox API quota. | The 6-hour S3 cycle is operationally necessary (a billing run or lease close 5.5 hours ago must be recoverable without re-entering data). The Dropbox destination is a safety net against full S3 unavailability, not a hot standby — daily granularity is acceptable for that threat model. Storage tarball is already weekly (upload changes are slow); same cadence for Dropbox avoids a daily 100MB+ upload with no benefit. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1. |
| D-BACKUP-3 | Manual full backup is async: backup_runs row = job record → presigned S3 link (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1) | A manually-triggered full backup (DB + storage combined) cannot be synchronous — a combined dump + tar + upload can take 5-15 minutes. The design (implemented in S-BACKUP-3): (1) POST to a new endpoint creates a `backup_runs` row with status=in_progress and trigger_source=manual; (2) a background worker (proc_open → detached PHP subprocess) runs the actual dump/upload; (3) the row's status flips to success/failed when the worker exits; (4) the UI polls the row status and displays a presigned S3 download link on success. The `backup_runs` table introduced in S-BACKUP-1 is the job-record store for this async flow. | Synchronous backup via an HTTP request would time out for any realistic database size, and PHP max_execution_time is typically 30-60s. The async job-record pattern is the only viable approach. The presigned-link delivery (vs email) keeps the file access within the existing auth perimeter and avoids the complexity of email attachments for potentially large files. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-1. |
| D-BACKUP-4 | Dropbox cron mirrors the latest S3 artifact; never creates a second dump (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-2) | `cron/backup_dropbox.php` calls `BackupRun::lastSuccess('s3', type)` to find the most recently uploaded S3 file, then downloads it via `StorageClient::download()` to a temp file and uploads it to Dropbox via `DropboxClient::upload()`. If no S3 artifact is found, it writes a failed `backup_runs` row with `error_message='no source artifact'` and exits 0 cleanly (fail-soft). This design ensures Dropbox always carries exactly what S3 already verified, with no independent dump logic. | Creating an independent dump would: (a) double the load on the prod DB for every Dropbox run; (b) produce a slightly different snapshot than the S3 copy (race window); (c) require the cron to own dump logic already encapsulated in backup_db.php. Mirroring is simpler, cheaper, and guarantees bit-for-bit consistency with the S3 artifact. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-2. |
| D-BACKUP-7 | Manual full backup bundles the latest s3/db + s3/storage artifacts (no re-dump); backup_runs row IS the job record (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-3c) | The async manual "download everything" worker (`cron/backup_manual_worker.php`) does NOT generate fresh dumps — it locates the latest `s3/db` and `s3/storage` artifacts via `BackupRun::lastSuccess`, downloads them through StorageClient, and tars them (NO `-z` — members are already gzipped) into `backups/manual/manual_<ts>.tar`. The enqueue endpoint opens a `manual/full` in_progress `backup_runs` row (the job record — no separate queue table); the worker flips it to success/failed; the UI polls `status.php` then `download.php` (fresh 5-min presigned link). If either source artifact is missing → fail-soft 'no source artifact' row. Retention keeps the last `MANUAL_BACKUP_RETENTION_COPIES` (env, default 5). | Re-dumping would double prod DB load and could produce a snapshot inconsistent with what S3 already verified; bundling the verified artifacts is cheaper and consistent (same rationale as D-BACKUP-4 for the Dropbox mirror). Reusing `backup_runs` as the job record avoids a new table and gives manual backups the same history/audit trail as the cron destinations. A synchronous HTTP build would time out (PHP max_execution_time); the enqueue→worker→poll→presigned-download flow is the only viable shape. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-3c. |
| D-BACKUP-6 | Storage backup gathers user content through StorageClient (driver-agnostic), never a hardcoded local dir (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-3a) | `cron/backup_storage.php` lists every key via `StorageClient::listByPrefix('')`, excludes `backups/` + `db-backups/` via the pure `ff_storage_backup_should_include()`, downloads each kept key into a staging dir via `StorageClient::download()`, then tars + uploads. There is NO `STORAGE_DRIVER` branch — dev (local) and prod (s3) run the identical path. A 0-content result is a SUCCESS (valid near-empty tarball + success backup_runs row), not an error. | The prior version tarred the LOCAL `storage/uploads/` dir. On prod (`STORAGE_DRIVER=s3`) that dir is empty because real uploads live in S3, so the storage backup silently captured 0 files — and the Dropbox storage mirror + future manual full backup inherited the emptiness. Gathering through the abstraction is the only way the backup is correct under BOTH drivers, and it makes the dev smoke exercise the real prod gather path (a hardcoded-local-dir backup can't be tested for the s3 case in dev). Same failure class as Traps 70/71/72 (REFERENCE.md Trap 73). Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-3a. |
| D-BACKUP-5 | Dropbox uses app-folder access; paths /db and /storage; retention via env (default 30 DB / 12 storage) (locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-2) | The Dropbox app should be registered in the App Console with App folder access (not Full Dropbox). Backup files are written to `{dropbox.folder_path}/{type}/{filename}` where `type` is `db` or `storage` and `dropbox.folder_path` defaults to `/FleetForge Backups`. Retention is configured via env vars: `DROPBOX_DB_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30 — delete DB files older than N days) and `DROPBOX_STORAGE_RETENTION_COPIES` (default 12 — keep the N most recent storage tarballs). The retention function is fail-soft: a cleanup error is logged but never fails the backup run that just succeeded. | App-folder access limits the app to its own folder (`/Apps/{AppName}/`) instead of the full Dropbox — minimum-privilege principle; prevents a compromised refresh token from reading or deleting unrelated files. The env-var retention approach matches the existing S3 cron pattern (`BACKUP_DB_RETENTION_DAYS`, `BACKUP_STORAGE_RETENTION_MONTHS`) and allows per-environment overrides without code changes. Locked 2026-06-06 via S-BACKUP-2. |
| D-PICKER-ENDPOINT-ROOT-RELATIVE | FF_RecordPicker `endpoint` is a ROOT-RELATIVE path (`/api/v1/…`), never `base_url(...)`; `FF_Api.url()` owns the base-path prefix and is idempotent against already-absolute URLs (locked 2026-06-07 via S-FIX-SELECTORS-EMPTY) | A picker config passes `endpoint` as a root-relative path. `FF_RecordPicker.search()`/`fetchInitial()` wrap it in `FF_Api.url()`, which prepends `window.FF_BASE_PATH`. Passing `base_url('api/v1/…')` (already a fully-qualified `https://host/fleetforge/api/v1/…`) double-prefixes to `/fleetforgehttps://…` → 404 → the picker's `try/catch` swallows the JSON parse failure into `results=[]` → silent empty selector. The gold-standard forms (credit_notes/payments/reservations) already use root-relative endpoints. `FF_Api.url()` now returns an already-absolute `http(s)://` URL untouched so a future slip can't 404. Contrast: direct `fetch()`/`FF_Api.get()`/`FF_Api.post()` calls (which do NOT wrap in `FF_Api.url()`) correctly take a `base_url(...)` absolute URL — the root-relative rule is specific to `FF_RecordPicker` `endpoint`. Guarded by `tests/_smoke_selector_endpoints.php` PART A. | One shared cause produced empty selectors on 7 forms (17 picker instances) while the backend was 100% healthy — invisible to every server-side smoke. Standardizing on root-relative picker endpoints + an idempotent `FF_Api.url()` + a static smoke guard closes the class so a `base_url()` slip fails CI instead of silently shipping an empty picker. Locked 2026-06-07 via S-FIX-SELECTORS-EMPTY. |

## KEY LEARNINGS — searchable index

Standalone index of cross-session lessons learned. SESSION LOG entries above retain their per-session learnings inline (chronological narrative); this section is the searchable subject-by-subject index. Add a new K-* entry when a learning surfaces that's likely to apply across sessions, not just the one that surfaced it.

| # | Date | Subject | Learning |
|---|------|---------|----------|
| K-1 | 2026-05-07 | **Namespace mismatch bug pattern** (S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE) | When a docblock asserts a column contract that doesn't match actual data convention, the upstream lookup chain silently fails (returns NULL or zero rows; downstream consumers see "no match" as a fall-through, not as an error). Fix protocol: (1) scan ALL writers + readers to identify the dominant convention — don't trust the docblock. (2) Align the outlier (usually the queries, not the data — cheaper, no migration). (3) Update the docblock to match reality, with WHY the prior claim was wrong so the next reader knows the trap. (4) Add test coverage proving the lookup yields expected results for production cases, including a CONTROL assertion that the pre-fix query shape returns 0 rows on live data — without this control, a future test reader cannot tell whether the chain "always worked" or was silently broken before the fix. (5) Lock the canonical contract as a D-* decision in PROGRESS.md DECISIONS table AND cite it in REFERENCE.md §0 LOCKED DECISIONS for quick-lookup discoverability. Pattern surfaced in S-LOOKUP-RATES-NAMESPACE: `lookup_rates.php` was the outlier against the dominant category convention; data was already 100% category-form so zero migration needed; D134 locked the contract going forward. |
| K-11 | 2026-05-07 | **Lock multi-agent discipline before frequency, not after** (S-MULTI-AGENT-DISCIPLINE-IMPL) | K-6 (S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX same-session overlap, 2026-05-07) was one data point in 177 commits — caught and reconciled cleanly because the parallel edits were additive (two non-overlapping I6 stress tests, additive REFERENCE.md sections, no migration conflicts). The failure modes of (c) accept-and-reconcile escalate non-linearly with concurrency: two agents both ALTER TABLE the same column would corrupt the schema before D131 parity smoke runs. The asymmetry between cost-of-discipline (low: one status field + a pre-flight read) and cost-of-the-second-incident (high: schema corruption, manual DB recovery) means the discipline should be locked at the first incident, not the tenth. Pattern: when a new incident class first appears, run the failure-mode analysis immediately and surface the discipline question — don't wait for recurrence to validate "this is a pattern." S-ACCT-AUDIT (b74b947, same day, different parallel session, SESSION LOG row backfilled in this same commit) confirms the first incident wasn't isolated — concurrency is happening, just not always with conflicts yet. |
| K-13 | 2026-05-11 | **Global include CSS as universal print concern, not page-scoped** (S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE C3-T1-FIX) | When a CSS class is rendered globally — via `includes/header.php`, `includes/footer.php`, `includes/partials/*` — its print-time behavior is a universal concern across every admin page that uses the standard layout. Hide rules belong in the GLOBAL `@media print` block in `public/assets/css/app.css`, NOT in per-page page-scoped `<style>` blocks. The page-scoped print block is for elements unique to that page (e.g., the invoice's letterhead, financial summary card, line items table). Surfaced via the `.search-modal` (a.k.a. `#ff-search-modal`) incident in S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE T1: search modal is rendered globally via `includes/footer.php` on every admin page; uses Alpine `x-show="open"` for visibility (default `open: false`). When the modal is open at print time — or Alpine fails to apply hide before the print engine captures the DOM — its `.search-overlay` child paints `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` over the entire viewport, producing a dark semi-transparent overlay. The page-scoped `@media print` in `show.php` hid `.modal-overlay` (covering void/delete/confirm/email modals) but NOT `.search-modal` — a page-scoped fix would have hidden the overlay on /invoices/show only, leaving every OTHER admin page's print still broken. The right fix is one-line in app.css's `@media print` hide list adding `.search-modal, .search-overlay, .modal-overlay, .modal-backdrop, .sidebar-overlay`. Pattern: when adding `@media print` hide rules, ask "is this class rendered by an include?" If yes → app.css `@media print`. If no → page-scoped `<style>`. Diagnostic: grep `class="<X>"` across `includes/` to determine universality before scoping the fix. The cost-of-discipline (one extra grep at fix-time) versus cost-of-no-discipline (universal bug fixed per-page, only the page that surfaced the bug benefits, every other admin print still ships the regression). |
| K-12 | 2026-05-07 | **Documentation divergence is its own bug class** (S-DOC-STATUS-RECONCILE-CLOSE) | S-QUEUE-STATUS-RECONCILE diagnostic surfaced 4 cases where actual ship state (git log + commits) diverged from declared state (CURRENT_SESSIONS.md status / PROGRESS.md SESSION LOG). Cause: post-ship doc updates were skipped or partial during fast session cycling. Cost-of-divergence: operator confusion ("did this ship?"), planning errors ("let me draft this — wait it's already done"), audit trail gaps. The S-QUEUE-STATUS-RECONCILE diagnostic should run periodically (e.g. end of each work day or every N sessions) to catch divergence before it accumulates. Two-sided protocol. |
| K-14 | 2026-05-12 | **Category separation in tracking files — pre-deploy obligations need their own canonical file** (S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE) | K-12 ("documentation divergence is its own bug class") established that tracking-file state must match reality. K-14 extends K-12 with a category-separation rule: tracking files have shapes, and filing an item in the wrong-shaped file is itself documentation divergence. Three categories with three canonical files: **(a) bug-shaped** — a defect in shipped code — files to `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` → KNOWN ISSUES (`#NNN`); **(b) session-shaped** — work that will be a future session — files to `FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md` queue; **(c) pre-deploy-shaped** — a `.env` key needing a real prod value, an AWS resource to provision, a DNS record, a smoke/rollback procedure, a monitoring dashboard, a data-state precondition — files to `FLEETFORGE_PREDEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md` in the appropriate category (A asset cache / B prod .env keys / C DNS / D AWS infra / E data migrations / F accounting state / G smoke / H rollback / I monitoring / J references). **Why this surfaced as a discipline gap:** before S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE there was no canonical pre-deploy file, so pre-deploy obligations accumulated under the wrong categories — `FF_ASSET_VERSION` bumps got noted in SESSION LOG narrative but had no actionable home, AR drift reconciliation was filed as a fix-script with no deploy-time pointer, AWS resource provisioning was scattered across SPEC_FINAL.md + REFERENCE.md + runbooks. Operator pre-work for the cutover would have to walk multiple files cold to find every obligation. **The discipline is two-sided:** (i) when filing a new obligation, route it to the correct file category before writing; (ii) when reading any tracking file, the file's stated category defines what belongs there — a pre-deploy obligation in KNOWN ISSUES is misfiled even if the entry is accurate. Both sides preserved K-12's "divergence is a bug class" framing — the shape of the entry must match the shape of the file. **Pattern for future tracking-file introductions:** when a new category of work-state surfaces that doesn't cleanly belong in any existing tracking file (and the existing files would have to bend their shape to absorb it), the right move is to introduce a new tracking file with its own discipline rule + inventory of pre-existing scattered items, not to overload an existing file. `FLEETFORGE_PREDEPLOY_CHECKLIST.md` is the first such addition since CURRENT_SESSIONS.md was created in S-CURRENT-SESSIONS-FILE. | K-15 | 2026-05-12 | **Data-path coverage discipline for code-class bug remediation** (S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX) | When a code-class bug is found and remediated for known affected rows, the remediation scope must include ALL rows produced by the buggy code path between bug introduction and bug fix. S-MILEAGE-ALLOWANCE-ZERO-FIX C5 remediated INV-91 via the same shape this session uses for INV-92, but didn't run the equivalent of pre-work scan #7 (full SELECT for ALL `mileage_adjustment` line items) to find OTHER rows produced by the same path. INV-92 had been created at 2026-05-06 22:11:16 via review_mileage.php approve flow — same code, same bug — and got missed. Going forward: when a code-path bug is found AND that path has produced any production data, the remediation pre-work scan must enumerate ALL rows from that path within the bug's lifetime window, not just the inciting row. Same discipline as D129 (re-run grep with NO scope filter before destructive ops) but for data-path coverage. Practical shape: identify the schema artifact the buggy code writes (here: `invoice_line_items.item_type='mileage_adjustment'`) + the time window (here: bug introduction in pre-history through fix commit), then `SELECT *` with no filters except the artifact + the lifetime window, surface all rows for operator decision. Cost: one query. Cost-of-skip: one row of $90.08 under-billing slipped past one full session. The asymmetry favors the discipline. |

| K-17 | 2026-05-12 | **Branch divergence reconciliation discipline — merge commit, not rebase, when journal files are in scope** (S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE) | When a worktree branch (D136 isolation) and main both accumulate commits independently AND both sides touch live-state-tracking files (`FLEETFORGE_CURRENT_SESSIONS.md`, `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` SESSION LOG / Recent ship history / KEY LEARNINGS, or any file functioning as a journal of mutable state), **rebase is the wrong tool** — replay-of-historical-snapshots will force conflicts at every commit that touched the journal because each commit captured the journal at a different moment-in-time. **Use merge commit instead**: git's three-way merge handles journal-style files cleanly — single 3-way merge produces editorial-merge decisions (which entries to keep, which order), not impossible reconciliations. Non-linear history is honest representation of genuinely parallel work, not noise. **Pre-merge:** tag the worktree branch as safety net (`pre-rebase-<S-LABEL>-backup` style, push to origin for 30 days), inventory SHA cross-references in canonical docs (none are load-bearing as click-through links — historical narrative refs are time-locked per S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE convention, do not update). **Post-merge:** manual chronological reconciliation of the journal sections (Recent ship history descending UTC within date; SESSION LOG ascending UTC; KEY LEARNINGS table by K-number convention not strict chronology); surface each conflict hunk verbatim BEFORE applying resolutions; operator confirms each. **Origin:** S-FORK-CLOSE-RESOLVE 2026-05-12, when rebase aborted at commit 2/11 due to journal-file conflicts on `claude/kind-sanderson-4ed75d` worktree branch (S-DOCS-CLUSTER + S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE + S-PREDEPLOY-CHECKLIST-CREATE arcs accumulating in parallel with S-REVIEW-MILEAGE-TAX-FIX on main). Switched to Option B merge commit (ab122eb) and resolved cleanly with 4 conflict hunks across 2 files. **Rebase remains the right tool** for code-only divergence (no journal files in the diverged commits); **merge commit is the right tool** when journal files are in scope. Pre-rebase / pre-merge backup tag is free safety (cost-of-discipline: 10s; cost-of-no-discipline: manual `git reflog` archaeology when something goes sideways). Diagnostic at decision time: `git diff <base>...<branch> -- '<journal-files>'` — if non-empty, prefer merge commit; if empty, rebase is safe. |
| K-18 | 2026-05-12 | **Stress test pre-population can hide bugs in fallback paths** (S-MILEAGE-2B C3.5) | When introducing a fallback gate (e.g., "if caller didn't pre-populate X, fetch X from upstream service"), the happy-path stress test that pre-populates X correctly bypasses the fallback codepath entirely — exercising only the "caller supplied X" branch. The fallback branch can ship broken (e.g., my C3 InvoiceGenerator change accessed `$lease['samsara_vehicle_id']` but the column lives on `equipment_units`, not `leases` — silent null → fallback never fired) and the stress will pass. **Pattern:** when introducing a fallback gate, also write a stress case that explicitly exercises the fallback path (no pre-population + upstream condition that triggers the fetch + assertion that the fetch ran). The 5 cases in `tests/_stress_drawdown_emit.php` all pre-populated `odometer_at_period_*_km` AND created leases without `samsara_vehicle_id` (the lease table doesn't even have the column — it's on `equipment_units`). Either of those guards short-circuits the Samsara fallback, so the broken JOIN bug never surfaced through the stress. Surfaced during pre-C4 INV-87 lookup that selected `l.samsara_vehicle_id` and crashed with "Unknown column" — that's when the bug was caught. Fix landed in C3.5 (commit 64b37cb) with a `LEFT JOIN equipment_units` extension to the lease SELECT. **K-15 adjacency:** K-15 is data-path coverage discipline ("when a code-class bug is found, remediate ALL rows produced by that path"). K-18 is the test-design parallel ("when adding a fallback gate, write a test that proves the fallback works"). Both rest on the discipline "the test that PASSES says nothing about the paths it didn't exercise." Cost of K-18: one additional stress case per fallback introduction. Cost of no K-18: silent production failure in 100% of fallback-eligible invocations. |

FOR UPDATE` — not use the cached `$lease` array value from the close transaction's opening SELECT. **Origin:** S-MILEAGE-3 C3 placed the refund dispatch block AFTER the lease-close audit_log row but BEFORE the ADV-BILL-1 advance handling + legacy partial-end final-invoice generation. Then the final-invoice generation ran createFromLease, which independently fired the drawdown emit, consumed the same $77.78, and UPDATEd balance to $0. Customer outcome: $77.78 residual applied TWICE (drawdown credit on Invoice 3 + cash refund owed) → $155.56 total benefit from $77.78 residual. **Real financial double-credit, not a display artifact.** Surfaced at T1 Step 5 (KI #106 filed 2026-05-13 commit bda21ec); fixed in S-MILEAGE-3-FIX-0 by (a) moving the refund block to AFTER the final-invoice generation, (b) adding `$leasePostFinal = db_row("SELECT precharge_balance, precharge_refund_method FROM leases WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE", [$id])` re-read immediately before the dispatch logic, (c) keying needsRefund on the re-read $residualBalance rather than the cached $lease value. **Pattern for future close-time work:** if you're adding a block that reads/writes lease state in close.php, ask: "Does any invoice-generation call between transaction-open and this block mutate the column I'm reading?" If yes, re-read FOR UPDATE before consuming. Cost-of-discipline: one SELECT (~1ms). Cost-of-no-discipline: financial double-credit caught only via end-to-end T1 walk. **The smoke I9 invariant didn't catch this** because I9 keys on the persisted state (which was internally consistent: method='cash' + settled_at=NULL was valid), not on the relationship between refund amount and post-drawdown residual. A future I10 candidate: cross-check refund_amount in audit_log against post-final-drawdown precharge_balance — if amount > residual, fail. Locked here as discipline first; smoke candidate deferred to S-MILEAGE-5 scenario coverage. **I10 SHIPPED 2026-05-13 via S-MILEAGE-5** (commit e16d3f6 — both credit branch `credit_notes.amount == leases.precharge_balance` and cash branch `audit_log new_values.amount == leases.precharge_balance` paths, plus the S20 hermetic end-to-end scenario validating the post-drawdown identity holds through the full close-refund flow). |

| NAV-1 | 2026-04-07 | Accounting Nav Fixes (Topnav Dropdown Clipping + Sidebar Restructure) | **3 files modified, 0 new files.** Cross-cutting fix covering both the accounting topnav dropdown bug and the sidebar's accounting section. No new features — pure correctness + consistency. **(1) ROOT CAUSE — topnav dropdowns rendering empty**: `.acc-topnav` in `public/assets/css/app.css` used `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible`. Per CSS spec, setting `overflow-x` to any value other than `visible` silently forces `overflow-y` to a non-`visible` value (the browser computes it to `auto`), which creates a clipping context that hides the absolutely-positioned group dropdown panels. The HTML was correctly rendering all 16 child links (verified via curl), they were just visually clipped. **Fix**: replaced `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible` with `flex-wrap: wrap; overflow: visible`, allowing the nav pill-bar to wrap to a second row on narrow viewports instead of scrolling horizontally, and letting the dropdown panels escape the container cleanly. Added an explanatory comment block about the CSS spec gotcha for future maintainers. **(2) Sidebar accounting section restructured to mirror topnav**: the sidebar previously had 8 individual items (Dashboard, Chart of Accounts, Journal Entries, Accounts Payable, Bank, Tax, Reports, Budgets) — of which 4 (`/accounting/accounts-payable`, `/accounting/tax`, `/accounting/reports`, `/accounting/budgets`) were dead 404s, and the structure didn't match the grouped topnav built in S028-c. Replaced entire accounting section in `config/navigation.php` with a single collapsible "Accounting" parent item (`calculator` icon, `match_prefix => '/accounting'`) containing 8 children: Dashboard, General Ledger, Receivables, Payables, Banking, Fixed Assets, Periods, Settings — exactly matching the 6 functional groups + Periods + Settings in the topnav. Each group child uses a `match_prefix` array listing all sibling URLs so the child stays highlighted across every sub-page in its group (e.g. "General Ledger" child is active on `/accounting/ledger`, `/accounting/chart-of-accounts`, `/accounting/journal-entries`, and `/accounting/reports/trial-balance`). Permissions use the correct module keys: `journal_entries` for Dashboard/GL/Receivables/Settings, `accounts_payable` for Payables, `bank_accounts` for Banking, `fixed_assets` for Fixed Assets, `period_management` for Periods. **(3) `match_prefix` field added to `includes/sidebar.php`**: backward-compatible enhancement — any nav item (parent or child) can now declare an optional `match_prefix` field as either a single string or an array of strings; the active-state detection iterates the prefix list and activates on the first match via `str_starts_with($_currentPath, FF_BASE_PATH . $_mp)`. Falls back to `$_item['url']` when `match_prefix` is not set, so every existing nav item keeps working unchanged. Applied identically to parent active detection, child-active-expansion detection (with `break 2`), and the child render loop. Variable cleanup list updated: added `$_matchPrefixes`, `$_mp`, `$_childPrefixes`, `$_cp`; removed `$_itemFullUrl`, `$_childFullUrl`. **Verification**: (a) Standalone unit test `/tmp/ff_sidebar_test.php` — replicates the sidebar active-state logic against `config/navigation.php` without booting FleetForge, tests all 19 accounting URLs (`/accounting/dashboard`, `/chart-of-accounts`, `/journal-entries`, `/ledger`, `/reports/trial-balance`, `/ar-aging`, `/statements`, `/collections`, `/deposits`, `/bills`, `/ap-aging`, `/vendor-credits`, `/bank-accounts`, `/bank-reconciliation`, `/fixed-assets`, `/depreciation`, `/capex`, `/periods`, `/settings`) and asserts that parent is active + exactly one child is active + child label matches expected group → **19/19 PASS**. (b) HTTP-level test via curl+session against Herd — fetched all 19 pages and confirmed the correct sidebar child carries `is-active` class on every page. (c) Visual verification — Chrome headless screenshots of Fixed Assets, Chart of Accounts, and Statements pages confirming both topnav dropdowns open correctly (no clipping) AND sidebar group highlight synchronizes with the topnav group. **Files modified**: `public/assets/css/app.css` (topnav overflow), `includes/sidebar.php` (match_prefix field), `config/navigation.php` (accounting section restructure). **SC passed**: SC1 php -l all modified files clean ✅; SC2 unit test 19/19 pages pass ✅; SC3 HTTP 19/19 pages render correct sidebar highlight ✅; SC4 topnav dropdown panels visible and not clipped on narrow + wide viewports ✅; SC5 all sidebar child URLs resolve to real pages (no more 404s) ✅. |

| VALID-2 | 2026-04-07 | Form Validation Messages (every form, every field, every accounting page) | **Cross-cutting pass completing what VALID-1 started — now every form in the admin app accumulates field-level errors into a single `{success:false, error:{code:"VALIDATION_ERROR", message, fields:{...}}}` envelope, and every client page paints them into `.field-error` slots plus a `.form-error-banner` at the top of the card/modal.** **(1) Accounting pages verified/fully wired** (15 files, ~400 `field-error`/`form-error-banner` markers total): `statements/index.php` (single Generate-Statement form — customer + date range + end≥start), `bank-accounts/index.php` (5 modals: Account / CSV Import / Manual Txn / Transfer / NSF — 63 markers), `journal-entries/index.php` (Create JE modal with header fields + dynamic `lineErrors[]` parallel array + balance check `Math.abs(d-c) > 0.009` + regex parser `/^lines[\.\[](\d+)[\]\.](.+)$/` to map server `lines[N].field` keys back to UI), `bank-reconciliation/index.php` (Start New Recon form), `depreciation/index.php` (Generate Preview modal), `capex/index.php` (4 forms: Create / Complete / Capitalize / Expense — strips `asset_data.` prefix from server keys), `fixed-assets/index.php` (4 modals: Dispose / Impair / Create / Edit — STALE_DATA friendly message, GL account + depreciation method + salvage value rules, payoff fields with financing_rate ≤ 1), `tax/index.php` (Create Period / Mark Filed / Remit modals — tax_type ∈ {gst_hst,pst_bc,pst_sk,pst_mb}, frequency ∈ {monthly,quarterly,annually}, period_end≥period_start, spec-exact messages), `settings/index.php` (5 tabs with per-tab `formErrors` banner + `errors` per-field: general/capex_threshold / depreciation method+life+salvage / tax_filing gst+pst frequency + server key prefix stripping), `bills/index.php`, `vendor-credits/index.php`, `deposits/index.php`, `collections/index.php`, `categorization-rules/index.php`, `chart-of-accounts/index.php`. All 15 accounting pages have: per-form `FormError` banner key + `Errors` object, helpers `_extractError(r, fallback)` + `_clearErrors(errorsObj, bannerKey)` + `_paintErrors(errorsObj, bannerKey, r, fallback)` iterating `r.error.fields` and routing `_general` to the banner, client-side `validateXxx()` mirroring API field rules, `:class="errors.X ? 'is-invalid' : ''"` input highlighting, `@input`/`@change="errors.X = ''"` self-clearing, and `_paintErrors` called in the `!r.success` branch of every submit handler. **(2) Server API bugs fixed during smoke test** — two endpoints were emitting non-VALID-2 envelopes and got rewritten: **(a) `api/v1/vendors/create.php`** was failing fast with `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …)` and single-field `VALIDATION_ERROR` messages on every guard (name, vendor_type, rating, hourly_rate) — refactored to accumulate every error into a `$fields[]` array, check email format via `clean_email()`, validate hourly_rate ≥ 0, and emit one `json_validation_error($fields)` at the end; duplicate-name uniqueness now also reports through the fields envelope so the client highlights the name field. **(b) `api/v1/yards/create.php`** was using a bespoke `['errors' => [...]]` extra key instead of the standard `fields` + was failing fast on `name` — refactored to accumulate errors (`name`, `capacity` non-negative, `manager_id` existence), emit `json_validation_error($fields)` once, and report name collisions through the same envelope. **(3) Smoke test harness** — `tests/_smoke_valid2.php` (NEW, ~290 lines). Manually writes a real PHP session file to `/var/tmp/sess_<id>` (the path Herd's PHP-FPM uses — **not** CLI PHP's `/var/folders/x6/.../T/`), injects `ff_user` + `ff_last_activity` + a known `csrf_token`, then uses `curl_init()` to POST bad JSON payloads against the live Herd endpoints with `Cookie: ff_session=<id>` + `X-CSRF-Token: <csrf>`. **30 test cases run**, covering every create endpoint in the app: Journal Entry (empty / 1 line / unbalanced), Bank Account (empty / bad currency), Bank Transfer (same source/dest), Bill (empty), Tax Period (bad tax_type / end-before-start), CapEx Request, Vendor Credit, AR Deposit, Customer (empty / bad email / discount > 100 / negative credit limit), Equipment Unit (empty / bad year), Lease, Invoice (empty / period_end before period_start), Payment (empty / negative amount), Vendor, Reservation, Damage Claim, Maintenance WO, Inspection, Mileage Log, Yard. Each case asserts: (a) HTTP 422, (b) `success === false`, (c) `error.code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, (d) `error.fields` is a non-empty object containing the expected field keys. **Final run: 30 / 30 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP** — all envelopes shaped correctly, every expected field key present. Test file includes defensive cleanup that `DELETE`s any stray `company_name LIKE 'Smoke Acme%'` customers at the end so regressions can't leak rows into the dev DB. **(4) Standards reinforced**: `.form-error-banner` + `.field-error` CSS already shipped in VALID-1; `json_validation_error(array $fields, string $message)` in `api/bootstrap.php` is now the ONLY way form APIs should report validation errors (422, `error.code='VALIDATION_ERROR'`, `error.fields` map). `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …)` fail-fast pattern is retired for form endpoints. Every client submit handler follows the shape: `if (!this.validateX()) return; this.busy = true; try { const r = await FF_Api.post(...); if (r.success) { FF_Toast.success(...); this.xOpen = false; await this.load(); } else { this._paintErrors(this.xErrors, 'xFormError', r, '…'); } } catch(e) { this.xFormError = 'Network error. Please try again.'; } this.busy = false;`. **Stop conditions all ✅**: every form has field-level errors that appear inline (not just a top banner), every validation message is spec-exact, every server field key maps back to its UI slot, duplicate/lookup errors route to the offending field, the smoke test proves the envelope shape is identical across all 30 endpoints. |

## Model B Mileage Refactor — Multi-Session Master Plan

### Overview — Avi's intended Model B billing model
Optional per-lease precharge toggle. When `precharge_enabled=1`:
- Lease stores `precharge_amount` (operator-set, NOT derived from `estimated_mileage`) and running `precharge_balance`.
- Invoice 1 emits a visible "Mileage Precharge" line for the full `precharge_amount` — customer pays upfront.
- Each subsequent invoice (monthly cron OR ad-hoc manual) shows TWO visible mileage lines: usage at per-km/mile rate, and a precharge credit drawing the balance down. Net mileage = usage − credit.
- Balance decrements by the credit applied each period. When balance hits zero, future invoices bill straight per-km with no credit line.
- At lease close: positive remaining balance refunded via toggle — cash refund (DR AR / CR Cash) or account credit (credit_note row, `source='mileage_overpayment'`). One-time customers' unused credits must be convertible to cash later.

Customers without precharge (`precharge_enabled=0`): straight per-km billing each invoice, no allowance, no review gate, no drawdown logic. Model B Lite (D135 configuration).

### Session breakdown

|---------|-------|--------|--------|
| S-MILEAGE-2A | Invoice 1 precharge line + activation balance init | ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-12 | ~90 min |
| S-MILEAGE-2B | Drawdown on subsequent invoices + Model C retirement + Drawdown Reconciliation panel + spec rewrite | ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-12 | ~3 hrs (9.5-commit arc) |
| S-MILEAGE-3 | Lease close + cash/credit refund toggle + retire priorExcessKm safeguard from S-MILEAGE-FIX-0 + ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md rewrite | QUEUED (depends on 2B) | ~90 min |
