| S-MILEAGE-4 | Placeholder — may dissolve into 2B/3; remove from queue when confirmed | PLACEHOLDER | TBD |

### Dispatch contract reference
S-INVOICE-DISPLAY-COMPREHENSIVE (commits 8bc4e5c + aabb087 + 5dc2af2 + df1bd20 + f9130a2 + ea98362 — see SESSION LOG entry on 2026-05-11; brought to main via merge commit ab122eb on 2026-05-12) placed forward-looking markers **exclusively in app/admin/invoices/show.php** (InvoiceGenerator.php was NOT touched in that arc):

- **LINE TYPE DISPATCH CONTRACT comment block** at app/admin/invoices/show.php:1866-1906 (comment 1866-1886 + `$itemTypeBadge` match table 1889-1906).
  - Current supported item_type values (from show.php:1879-1881 + DB ENUM at FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql:1898): `base_rental`, `mileage_precharge`, `mileage_adjustment`, `mileage_credit`, `insurance`, `warranty`, `late_fee`, `early_return_credit`, `manual_adjustment`, `damage`, `discount`, `account_credit_applied`, `other`, `gps` (14 values).
  - Pending types per show.php:1882-1885 (S-MILEAGE-2B scope): `mileage_drawdown_credit`, `mileage_usage`.
  - Note: `mileage_precharge` is supported in display but NOT EMITTED by any production code today (per S-MILEAGE-MODEL-AUDIT 2026-05-04). S-MILEAGE-2A is the first production emit path.
- **Dual S-MILEAGE-2A/2B extension point markers** in show.php:
  - PHP-side at lines 1769-1782 (taxable subtotal docblock with explicit "S-MILEAGE-2A/2B note" at 1775-1781)
  - HTML-side at line 2182 (template comment: "Model B mileage breakdown (usage − credit) slots here between line items aggregate and tax block")
- **lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php** carries NO S-MILEAGE-2A/2B markers today. S-MILEAGE-2A will place engine-side markers at the precharge emit site as part of that work.

Each session in the refactor arc extends these dispatch contracts before adding business logic. New line type → confirm ENUM value exists (or add migration) → confirm match case exists (or add case) → confirm display template handles the shape → wire engine emit → add tests.

### Hybrid state contract
Between 2A ship and 2B ship, FleetForge is in hybrid Model B/C state:
- `precharge_enabled=1` leases: Invoice 1 is Model B (precharge line). Invoice 2+ is Model C (per-period excess gate). Live-coherent by design.
- `precharge_enabled=0` leases: All invoices use Model B Lite (straight per-km, no excess gate if `estimated_mileage=0`) per D135.
- Model C scaffolding (S-LEASE-MILEAGE manager review gate, priorExcessKm safeguard): NOT deleted until S-MILEAGE-3. The priorExcessKm safeguard in particular must survive until S-MILEAGE-3 explicitly retires it.

### Out-of-scope-but-tracked items
- Bug 1: "Cumulative Total" label on invoice show page is misleading (should read "Lease-to-Date Distance"). Rider on S-MILEAGE-2B.
- Bug 4: soft validation when `billing_period_start < lease.start_date`. Rider on S-MILEAGE-2B.
- Close-time refund toggle (cash vs credit): S-MILEAGE-3.
- Customer portal rendering of precharge balance: S-MILEAGE-4 placeholder.
- priorExcessKm safeguard deletion: S-MILEAGE-3 (NOT 2B).

### Test strategy
- Per-session integration tests: each session in the arc includes its own T8/T10/T12 integration tests.
- Scenario test suite: S-MILEAGE-5 ships 20 hermetic scenarios using SamsaraClient fixture mode (FIX_STD, FIX_PARKED, FIX_NONE, FIX_RESET, FIX_SPARSE, FIX_GAP per lib/Samsara/FixtureProvider.php).
- D132 extension: S-MILEAGE-2A must extend the rate-tier completeness invariant to cover `precharge_amount` when `precharge_enabled=1` (smoke invariant I7). DB-side `chk_leases_precharge_amount` CHECK at FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql:2248 already enforces; I7 makes the gate doc-asserted by the smoke suite, not only DB-asserted by the CHECK.
- Fixture mode flag: settings key `samsara.fixture_mode` (lib/GPS/SamsaraClient.php:1259 dispatch path) — set to `'1'` (string) in all test contexts; reset on exit. Never test against live Samsara.

DB_SANITIZE_COLUMN (S016):

FF_API.POST:

CSRF TRAP: Raw fetch() MUST include both headers:

S-PROD-1B KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • D14 invoice immutability is unconditional — no role exemption. The is_super_admin()
    check in the guard was a latent CRA compliance hole. Any future financial-field guard
    must apply to ALL callers without exception.
  • Full-PUT roundtrip pattern: when blocking a field post-send, compare submitted value
    against DB value rather than blocking on presence alone. Blocking notes by presence
    broke every form that re-posted the full invoice body unchanged.
  • Optimistic lock comparisons: NEVER use raw string equality on updated_at timestamps.
    Always normalise via DateTimeImmutable::getTimestamp() (Unix seconds). DST and driver
    microsecond padding both cause spurious 409s with raw string comparison.
  • MFA auto-set belongs at the role-mutation callsite, not in a migration. Any time
    users.role_id changes, recompute mfa_required from the new role's slug against
    security.mfa.required_roles. Demote lifts requirement only — never clear mfa_enabled
    or mfa_secret (D-E).
  • Reconcile scripts follow the S-FIX-2 pattern: default dry-run, --execute requires
    interactive 'yes', single db_transaction, per-row audit_log. Always audit dry-run
    output with the user before running --execute.

S-PROD-2 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • Sentry must be wired in bootstrap.php before session start so early crashes (DB
    connect fail, config parse error) are captured. Wiring it after auth means pre-auth
    errors are invisible in Sentry.
  • PII scrub in before_send needs TWO layers: key-name matching (password, api_key, etc.)
    AND value-pattern matching (bcrypt $2y$ prefix, ENC: AES ciphertext). Key-name alone
    misses secrets stored under unexpected keys; value-pattern alone is too broad.
  • SNS webhook contract: ALWAYS return HTTP 200 on valid signatures. Only 403 on sig
    failure. NEVER 5xx — SNS interprets that as a transient error and retries indefinitely,
    causing duplicate DB writes and audit log noise.
  • stream.php SSE compatibility: bootstrap.php sets Content-Type: application/json
    early, but stream.php overrides with Content-Type: text/event-stream before any output.
    The override is safe because PHP header() replaces rather than appends. Pre-SSE errors
    correctly use json_error(); post-SSE sendSSE() calls are a different format and must
    not be touched.
  • AI files had loaded config/app.php + auth.php directly, bypassing CSRF enforcement,
    Sentry capture, and json_error(). The correct pattern for all API files is
    bootstrap.php, which provides all of these. Direct config/auth loading is a red flag.
  • json_error() is a never-returning function — it calls exit() internally. Never add
    an explicit exit after it; doing so is dead code and misleads readers about control flow.

S-MILEAGE-1 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):

    Model A columns. All rows had mileage_precharge_amount=0.00 and
    mileage_precharge_invoiced=0. No real precharge data existed under Model A
    scaffolding — the audit's "zero writers" finding was substantively correct, but a
    default-value INSERT path was writing zeros on lease creation. Confirmed safe to
    proceed with Model B refactor. Backup table retained as audit trail; cleanup
    target post-S-MILEAGE-4.

S-CLEANUP-LBP-COLS-2 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):

    arc spanning S-MILEAGE-FIX-0 → S-MILEAGE-1 → S-CLEANUP-LBP-100 →
    S-CLEANUP-LBP-TABLE → S-CLEANUP-LBP-COLS-2. Four cleanup sessions to fully

    (the `lease_billing_periods` table itself, confirmed in S-CLEANUP-LBP-TABLE

  • Discipline stack validated end-to-end across the arc:
      D126 (master Edit appends at end on ADDs, symmetric remove on DROPs)

          enforced symmetric on every subsequent DROP session.

    cleanup phase.
  • Same-shape sessions become near-mechanical when the discipline stack is
    settled. S-CLEANUP-LBP-COLS-2's pre-work scan, decision sign-off, migration,
    master edit, parity gate, stress tests, and docs all matched
    S-CLEANUP-LBP-100's structure beat-for-beat. The brief explicitly named

    Future session-pattern reuse should follow this approach: name the
    template session in the brief, surface only the deltas, execute on rails.

S-CLEANUP-LBP-TABLE KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • Audit-scope-vs-general-usage gap (D129). When an audit's grep is scoped
    to a specific code path (e.g., mileage billing, accounting reconciliation,
    GPS sync), its "unused" findings are LOCAL to that path, not GLOBAL across
    the codebase. Before treating an audit's "X is unused" claim as actionable
    for a destructive operation (DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN at a key field),
    re-run the grep with NO scope filter. The S-MILEAGE-MODEL-AUDIT (Q4) said
    `lease_billing_periods` was unused — true within mileage paths, false in
    general (`InvoiceGenerator.php:656` writes one row per invoice;
    `invoices.billing_period_id` carries an active FK). Acting on the
    localized claim with a DROP TABLE would have failed at the FK constraint
    (ERROR 3730) AND broken every subsequent invoice generation.
  • Categorize grep hits by SCHEMA / HISTORY / PRODUCTION / TESTS / SCRIPTS
    before drafting any destructive op. The categorization makes production
    hits stand out so they can't be missed in a noisy hit list. For
    S-CLEANUP-LBP-TABLE: 34 hits across 10 files; 29 were schema/history/test
    noise; only 2 were production code — but those 2 (both in InvoiceGenerator)
    were conclusive on their own.
  • Live-DB row activity is a fast independent signal. If COUNT(*) > 0 with
    rows created in the last 30 days (or really, the last week), the table is
    being written to by SOMETHING. Combine with the FK dependency check
    (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE WHERE REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME = ?) for
    a complete picture in two SQL queries.
  • A clean "investigation only — no commits other than docs" outcome is a
    legitimate session shape. The audit report itself is the artifact; the
    docs commit is the audit's index entry. No migration, no code change, no
    schema change, no parity drift. Future investigative sessions chasing
    "is X really unused?" questions follow this template — pre-work scan +
    audit report in /tmp + docs commit referencing it + opened KNOWN ISSUE
    for the actual cleanup target if findings pivot.

S-CLEANUP-LBP-100 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • The D126/D127 schema discipline applies symmetrically to DROPs as well as
    ADDs. D126 said "append at end matching ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN semantics"
    for column adds; the inverse for drops is just "remove the column from
    wherever it lived" — the live DB doesn't reorder remaining columns when
    a DROP happens, and neither should the master file edit. Two surgical
    str_replace ops, no reordering. Parity smoke test catches drift either
    direction.
  • Trivial-data backup-skip pattern (D128) is the right call when ALL rows
    of the dropped columns carry zero/NULL/default values. Pre-session SELECT
    with COUNT + SUM aggregates is the gate. The S-MILEAGE-1 backup table
    precedent stays for the general case (any non-trivial row → snapshot it),
    but accumulating one dead backup table per drop session is its own kind
    of clutter. The migration's source code is the recoverable artifact when
    the data being preserved is structural-only.
  • Migration files are immutable historical record per the S-MIGRATIONS-RUNNER
    discipline. When grepping for column-name references during cleanup
    pre-work, hits in db_migrations/* are expected and untouchable — they
    document past work, not current schema. Filter them out of the
    "production references" count without further investigation.
  • Sibling-column scope discipline: when a session drops a pair of dead
    columns (e.g. `has_mileage_precharge` + `mileage_precharge_amount`), be
    explicit about whether parallel sibling pairs (e.g. `has_mileage_reconciliation`
    + `mileage_reconciliation_amount`) are in scope. The audit may have flagged
    BOTH pairs, but the brief should scope cleanly. S-CLEANUP-LBP-100
    explicitly preserved the reconciliation pair per brief; a future cleanup
    can drop them if Avi confirms the same trivial-data finding applies.

S-DATABASE-MASTER-RECONCILE-2 KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • In-place str_replace on the master file's CREATE TABLE column list does NOT
    match `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` semantics. ADD COLUMN (without BEFORE/AFTER)
    appends at the end of the column list; str_replace lands wherever the
    replaced text was. Always do schema column adds via two Edit calls — one
    to remove dropped columns at their position, one to append the new
    columns at the end (just before PRIMARY KEY / index/constraint declarations).
    The wrong pattern grep-verifies clean; the parity smoke test catches it.
  • The grep-only verification rule from D87 is necessary but not sufficient.
    `grep -c <new_column> FLEETFORGE_DATABASE_MASTER.sql >= 1` proves the
    column EXISTS but says nothing about its ordinal position, its CHECK
    constraint placement, its index ordering, or anything else that mysqldump
    would surface in a diff. Run `php tests/_smoke_master_schema_parity.php`
    at the end of every schema-touching session and confirm exit 0 BEFORE
    the final commit.
  • Trust but verify the brief premise. This session's brief assumed multiple
    sessions of accumulated drift (missing precharge cols, missing CHECK,
    missing S-LEASE-UNITS cols, missing SAMSARA-3 cols, missing
    schema_migrations). Reality: ALL of those were present in the master.
    The actual drift was 14 substantive lines — one column-ordering issue
    from a single session. Running the validation gate (round-trip dump-diff)
    BEFORE proposing a full regen surfaced the truth and avoided ~30 min of
    unnecessary regen ceremony + a 5400-line cosmetic diff. When a brief
    assumes a problem, run the cheapest verification that confirms or
    refutes the assumption before agreeing to the full remediation scope.
  • mysqldump round-trip noise is real and predictable. When master is
    re-loaded into a scratch DB and re-dumped, mysqldump emits redundant
    `CHARACTER SET utf8mb4` on every text column (matches the table-level
    default; the original master file omits it). Also: COMMENT clauses
    containing UTF-8 characters (em-dash, arrows) get mojibaked when
    `mysql <` is run without `--default-character-set=utf8mb4`. Both are
    cosmetic; both are filterable. The parity smoke test handles both
    automatically. Future ad-hoc loads of master should always pass
    `--default-character-set=utf8mb4` to avoid the comment mojibake.

S-MILEAGE-1B KEY LEARNINGS (apply forward):
  • Samsara docs verified mid-session contradicted Avi's brief on `gpsOdometerMeters`.
    Brief said "manually-editable for service intervals — not for billing"; current
    docs (https://developers.samsara.com/docs/calculating-distance-traveled-guide)
    describe it as a billing-grade #2 source (manual offset + GPS). Avi's exclusion
    call stands for now (simpler 2-tier preference: OBD → gps_distance), but if
    OBD-less trucks emerge in the fleet, this is the first thing to revisit.
  • audit_log.action ENUM still doesn't include 'samsara_history_query' (or any
    Samsara-specific action). Continuing the D102 workaround: action='cron' with
    descriptive entity_type='samsara_history_query'. If a future session adds enough
    Samsara/integration audit_log usage to justify, extending the ENUM is a one-line
    ALTER — cheaper than expanding the workaround across more callers.
  • Constructor BC migration pattern (D124): when introducing a new settings/env key
    naming convention, prefer the new keys via `?:` chain but fall back through the
    legacy keys in the constructor itself — single point of change benefits all
    methods on the client, ops can migrate at their own pace, and zero production
    impact at the deploy. Generalizes for any future renaming of integration keys
    (e.g. when SES bounces gain a `mailer.*` prefix migration, do the same).
  • Hermetic fixture mode design: dispatch hook lives at the very top of the
    production method, settings flag defaults to '0', strict string comparison
    against '1' (not loose `=== true`). Production cannot silently flip into fixture
    mode. The fixture provider returns the EXACT same shape as production (including
    bcmath conversion path) so tests exercise the contract end-to-end and float-leak
    bugs would be caught in fixture mode just as in live. T7 unit-conversion test
    confirmed: 1234.56 km → 767.12 miles bcmath-clean, no trailing-nines drift.
  • The smoke-test convention `tests/_smoke_*.php` carrying a final summary line
    "N/N passed in Xs" or "M/N passed (FAILED: T# name, ...)" is now grep-able for
    future CI integration. Apply this format to every new `_smoke_*.php` going
    forward — make CI integration cheap.
  • Tests that exercise the production HTTP loop (T8 pagination cap, T10 malformed
    response) cannot be exercised hermetically by a dispatch-at-the-top fixture
    mode by design. Document them as source-code-inspection tests (grep against the
    file for the expected guard text). Real coverage lands when the next session
    integrates the method into a caller (S-MILEAGE-2's invoice generation) and the
    integration tests can run against a mocked HTTP layer.

S035 KEY LEARNINGS (apply in S036):
  • dirname(__DIR__, N) — count slashes carefully when nesting API endpoints.
    /api/v1/accounting/X/index.php uses dirname(__DIR__, 4),
    /api/v1/accounting/X/Y/index.php uses dirname(__DIR__, 5).
    Both append '/api/bootstrap.php' (project root → /api/bootstrap.php).
  • Date math: NEVER use strtotime("$end +1 month") for end-of-month dates —
    Mar 31 +1 month → May 1 (rollover). Use DateTimeImmutable::modify('last day of +1 month').
  • §16 closed-period auto-redirect lands the JE in EARLIEST open period in the system
    (currentOpenPeriod ORDER BY year ASC, month ASC LIMIT 1), NOT the next open period
    after the original date. This is the convention shared with AutoEntryBridge::resolvePeriod.
    For tax remittances and any other §16 caller, set entry_date intentionally if you
    want a different placement.
  • Tax management is in place: acc_tax_filing_periods + acc_tax_remittances + 6 service
    methods + 6 API endpoints. Future PASS-12 tax UI hook into TaxFilingService::listPeriods
    and getPeriodDetail to fetch totals and drill-down rows.

# AWS SETUP GUIDE

> Follow these steps in order. You are at: **Step 1 — AWS console just opened.**

---

## STEP 1 — Create the Lightsail Instance

1. Go to **lightsail.aws.amazon.com**
2. Click **"Create instance"**
3. Configure:
   - **Region:** `us-west-2` (Oregon) — closest to BC/Canada west coast
   - **Platform:** Linux/Unix
   - **Blueprint:** OS Only → **Ubuntu 22.04 LTS** — do NOT use LAMP blueprint
   - **Launch script:** Leave empty
   - **SSH key pair:** Create new → **download the .pem file and save it permanently** — cannot be re-downloaded
   - **Plan:** **$20/month** (4 GB RAM, 2 vCPU, 80 GB SSD) — do not go cheaper
   - **Instance name:** `fleetforge-prod`
4. Click **"Create instance"** — wait ~2 minutes until status shows "Running"

---

## STEP 2 — Attach a Static IP

1. Lightsail console → **Networking** tab (left sidebar)
2. Click **"Create static IP"**
3. Attach to: `fleetforge-prod`
4. Name: `fleetforge-static-ip`
5. Click **"Create and attach"**
6. **Write down this IP address** — needed for DNS and SSH

---

## STEP 3 — Configure Firewall

1. Click `fleetforge-prod` → **Networking** tab → Firewall section
2. Set rules exactly:
   - ✅ SSH — TCP — port 22 — **Restrict to your IP** (click "Restrict to IP address")
   - ✅ HTTP — TCP — port 80 — Any IP
   - ✅ HTTPS — TCP — port 443 — Any IP
   - ❌ Remove any other rules
3. Save

> **Why:** Port 22 open to the world gets brute-forced within hours.

---

## STEP 4 — Point Your Domain to the Static IP

**If your domain is at an external registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap, etc.):**
- Add A record: `@` → your static IP
- Add A record: `www` → your static IP
- DNS propagation: 5–30 minutes

**If buying a new domain via Route 53:**
- AWS console → Route 53 → Register Domain
- After registration → Hosted Zones → your domain → Create Record → A record → static IP

> Test: `ping yourdomain.com` should return your static IP before proceeding to Step 12 (SSL).

---

## STEP 5 — SSH Into the Server

```bash
# On your local machine
chmod 400 ~/path/to/your-key.pem
ssh -i ~/path/to/your-key.pem ubuntu@YOUR_STATIC_IP
```

---

## STEP 6 — Install PHP 8.2 + Apache + MySQL

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y software-properties-common
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:ondrej/php -y
sudo apt update

sudo apt install -y \
  php8.2 php8.2-mysql php8.2-mbstring php8.2-xml \
  php8.2-curl php8.2-zip php8.2-gd php8.2-intl \
  php8.2-opcache php8.2-bcmath \
  apache2 mysql-server git unzip curl

# Verify
php -v          # Must show 8.2.x
mysql --version # Must show 8.0.x
```

---

## STEP 7 — Configure PHP

```bash
sudo nano /etc/php/8.2/apache2/php.ini
```

Set these values (Ctrl+W to search):
```ini
memory_limit = 256M
upload_max_filesize = 25M
post_max_size = 30M
max_execution_time = 60
date.timezone = America/Vancouver
```

Save: Ctrl+X → Y → Enter

---

## STEP 8 — Set Up MySQL

```bash
sudo mysql_secure_installation
# Set strong root password, answer Y to all prompts

sudo mysql -u root -p
```

```sql
CREATE DATABASE fleetforge CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
CREATE USER 'fleetforge_user'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'STRONG_PASSWORD_HERE';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON fleetforge.* TO 'fleetforge_user'@'localhost';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
EXIT;
```

> Use a 20+ character random password. Store it in a password manager.

---

## STEP 9 — Install Composer

```bash
cd ~
curl -sS https://getcomposer.org/installer | php
sudo mv composer.phar /usr/local/bin/composer
composer --version  # Must show 2.x
```

---

## STEP 10 — Create Project Directories + Permissions

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/fleetforge
sudo chown ubuntu:ubuntu /var/www/fleetforge

# Create all required subdirectories
mkdir -p /var/www/fleetforge/storage/uploads/{customers,equipment,leases,inspections,damage,contracts,branding}
mkdir -p /var/www/fleetforge/storage/generated/{pdfs,exports,qrcodes}
mkdir -p /var/www/fleetforge/logs
mkdir -p /var/www/fleetforge/cache

# Block PHP execution in storage
echo 'Options -ExecCGI
AddHandler cgi-script .php .php3 .phtml .pl .py
php_flag engine off' | sudo tee /var/www/fleetforge/storage/.htaccess

# Backup directory
sudo mkdir -p /var/backups/fleetforge
sudo chown www-data:www-data /var/backups/fleetforge
```

## STEP 11 — Configure Apache Virtual Host

```bash
sudo nano /etc/apache2/sites-available/fleetforge.conf
```

Paste (replace `yourdomain.com`):
```apache
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    ServerAlias www.yourdomain.com
    DocumentRoot /var/www/fleetforge/public

    <Directory /var/www/fleetforge>
        Require all denied
    </Directory>

    <Directory /var/www/fleetforge/public>
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
        Options -Indexes
    </Directory>

    ErrorLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/fleetforge_error.log
    CustomLog ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/fleetforge_access.log combined
</VirtualHost>
```

```bash
sudo a2ensite fleetforge.conf
sudo a2dissite 000-default.conf
sudo a2enmod rewrite headers
sudo systemctl restart apache2
sudo systemctl status apache2   # Must show: active (running)
```

# BUILD PLAN — v4.0 ATOMIC SESSIONS

---

## THE SENIOR ENGINEER MINDSET

```
RULE 1: ONE VERIFIABLE THING PER SESSION
  A session is complete when one specific user-visible behaviour
  works correctly and all its failure modes are handled.
  Not "the customers module." Not "the API." 
  One thing. Fully working. Both sides. All edge cases.

RULE 2: CONTRACT BEFORE CODE
  Every session that builds an API endpoint starts with a written 
  contract. Claude Code writes the contract. You approve it. 
  Then and only then does code get written.
  Contract = exact request shape, exact response shape, 
             exact validation rules, exact error codes.

RULE 3: VERIFY THE FOUNDATION BEFORE BUILDING ON IT
  Before Session N+1 starts, Session N's output is re-tested.
  If it breaks, fix it before building anything on top of it.
  This is non-negotiable.

RULE 4: SAD PATH IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN HAPPY PATH
  The happy path usually works. It is the edge cases, the 
  concurrent requests, the missing data, the expired sessions,
  the 11MB files, the duplicate submissions — these are where
  production bugs live.

RULE 5: BUSINESS LOGIC LIVES IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE
  Validation: PHP only. JS validation is UX, not security.
  Billing math: lib/Billing/ pure classes only.
  State machines: API layer only. JS never transitions state.
  Permissions: PHP only. JS hiding is UX, not access control.

RULE 6: NO SESSION ENDS WITH "MOSTLY WORKING"
  If a test fails, fix it in the same session.
  If you cannot fix it, the session is not complete.
  Update PROGRESS with the exact failing test as a known issue.

RULE 7: THE CONTRACT IS THE SHARED TRUTH
  Frontend and backend implement against the same contract.
  When they disagree, the contract is updated, then both sides.
  Never let either side define reality unilaterally.
```

---

## SESSION OPENING TEMPLATE — MANDATORY EVERY SESSION

```
Read FLEETFORGE_SPEC_FINAL.md and FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md 
before writing a single line of code.

Verify: [state the specific thing from the last session that 
must still be working before we proceed]

Today's session: [single sentence describing the one thing 
we are building]

Step 1: Define the contract for this session (if it involves 
an API). Show me: exact endpoint, method, request fields, 
validation rules, success response shape, every error case 
with its HTTP status and error_code. Wait for my approval.

Step 2: After approval, build both sides (backend + frontend) 
against the approved contract.

Step 3: Run every test in the session's stop-condition list. 
Show me each result. Fix all failures before ending.

Step 4: Update FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md. Mark this session 
complete. Write the next session's opening instruction.
```

### S006 — DB Helper: Connection + Basic Queries
**One thing:** PDO connects. Basic CRUD helpers work. UTC enforced.
**Why split from other helpers:** DB connection is the most foundational dependency. If it's wrong, everything is wrong.

| Task | Status |
|------|--------|
| `includes/db.php` — PDO singleton | ✅ |
| Connection: charset=utf8mb4, emulate_prepares=false | ✅ |
| Connection: `SET time_zone = '+00:00'` on connect | ✅ |
| Connection: `SET NAMES utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci` | ✅ |
| `db_select(sql, params)` → array of rows | ✅ |
| `db_row(sql, params)` → single row or null | ✅ |
| `db_insert(table, data)` → last insert ID | ✅ |
| `db_update(table, data, where, whereParams)` → affected rows | ✅ |
| `db_execute(sql, params)` → affected rows | ✅ |
| `db_count(sql, params)` → int | ✅ |
| `db_exists(table, condition, params)` → bool | ✅ |
| All queries: parameterized — NEVER string interpolation | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```php
// Must ALL pass:
$id = db_insert('yards', ['name'=>'Test Yard','slug'=>'test-yard-'.time(),'is_active'=>1]);
assert(is_int($id) && $id > 0, 'insert must return int ID');

$row = db_row("SELECT * FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$id]);
assert($row['name'] === 'Test Yard', 'db_row must return correct row');
assert($row !== null, 'db_row must not return null for existing ID');

$null = db_row("SELECT * FROM yards WHERE id = 999999", []);
assert($null === null, 'db_row must return null for missing row');

$rows = db_select("SELECT * FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$id]);
assert(count($rows) === 1, 'db_select must return array');
assert($rows[0]['id'] === $id, 'db_select must return correct data');

$affected = db_update('yards', ['name'=>'Updated'], 'id = ?', [$id]);
assert($affected === 1, 'db_update must return affected row count');

$exists = db_exists('yards', 'id = ?', [$id]);
assert($exists === true, 'db_exists must return true for existing row');

$notExists = db_exists('yards', 'id = ?', [999999]);
assert($notExists === false, 'db_exists must return false for missing row');

$count = db_count("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$id]);
assert(is_int($count), 'db_count must return int');

// UTC timezone enforced
$tzRow = db_row("SELECT @@session.time_zone as tz", []);
assert($tzRow['tz'] === '+00:00', 'UTC timezone must be enforced on connection');

// Cleanup
db_execute("DELETE FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$id]);
echo "ALL DB BASIC TESTS PASSED\n";
```

---

### S007 — DB Helper: Transactions + Rollback
**One thing:** Transactions work. Rollback works. Partial writes are impossible.
**Why its own session:** Transaction integrity is the #1 protection against corrupt financial data. Verify this in complete isolation before billing code touches it.

| Task | Status |
|------|--------|
| `db_transaction(callable)` — wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT | ✅ |
| Auto-rollback on any exception thrown inside callable | ✅ |
| Re-throws exception after rollback | ✅ |
| Returns callable return value on success | ✅ |
| Nested transaction handling (savepoints) | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```php
// HAPPY PATH: both inserts commit
$result = db_transaction(function() {
    $id1 = db_insert('yards', ['name'=>'TX Test 1','slug'=>'tx-1-'.time(),'is_active'=>1]);
    $id2 = db_insert('yards', ['name'=>'TX Test 2','slug'=>'tx-2-'.time(),'is_active'=>1]);
    return [$id1, $id2];
});
assert(count($result) === 2, 'transaction must return callable result');
$check1 = db_row("SELECT id FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$result[0]]);
$check2 = db_row("SELECT id FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$result[1]]);
assert($check1 !== null, 'first insert must have committed');
assert($check2 !== null, 'second insert must have committed');
db_execute("DELETE FROM yards WHERE id IN (?,?)", $result);

// CRITICAL: rollback test — NOTHING must persist
$insertedId = null;
try {
    db_transaction(function() use (&$insertedId) {
        $insertedId = db_insert('yards', ['name'=>'Should Rollback','slug'=>'rollback-'.time(),'is_active'=>1]);
        throw new RuntimeException("Forced rollback");
    });
} catch (RuntimeException $e) {
    assert($e->getMessage() === "Forced rollback", 'exception must be re-thrown');
}
assert($insertedId !== null, 'ID was generated');
$rolled = db_row("SELECT id FROM yards WHERE id = ?", [$insertedId]);
assert($rolled === null, 'CRITICAL: rolled-back insert MUST NOT exist in DB');

echo "ALL TRANSACTION TESTS PASSED\n";
```

### S008 — Input Sanitization + Output Escaping Functions
**One thing:** Every input cleaning function is correct. Output escaping is bulletproof.
**Why its own session:** These are the #1 defence against XSS and injection. Get them right once, use everywhere.

| Task | Status |

| `includes/functions.php` (partial — sanitization only) | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```php
// e() — output escaping
assert(e('<script>alert(1)</script>') === '&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;');
assert(e("O'Brien") === "O&#039;Brien");
assert(e(null) === '');
assert(e(0) === '0');
assert(e('') === '');

// clean_string()
assert(clean_string('  hello  ') === 'hello');
assert(clean_string('<b>bold</b>') === 'bold');
assert(clean_string(str_repeat('a', 300), 255) === str_repeat('a', 255));
assert(clean_string(null) === null);

// clean_decimal() — strict
assert(clean_decimal('1234.56') === 1234.56);
assert(clean_decimal('$1,234.56') === null);  // formatted → null
assert(clean_decimal('1234') === 1234.0);
assert(clean_decimal('abc') === null);
assert(clean_decimal('') === null);
assert(clean_decimal(null) === null);
assert(clean_decimal('-100.50') === -100.50);  // negatives valid

// clean_date()
assert(clean_date('2025-03-21') === '2025-03-21');
assert(clean_date('2025-13-01') === null);     // month 13 invalid
assert(clean_date('2025-02-29') === null);     // 2025 not leap year
assert(clean_date('2024-02-29') === '2024-02-29'); // 2024 IS leap year
assert(clean_date('21/03/2025') === null);     // wrong format
assert(clean_date('') === null);

// clean_int()
assert(clean_int('42') === 42);
assert(clean_int('42.5') === null);            // floats rejected
assert(clean_int('-5') === -5);
assert(clean_int('abc') === null);
assert(clean_int('') === null);
assert(clean_int(0) === 0);

// clean_email()
assert(clean_email('user@example.com') !== null);
assert(clean_email('notanemail') === null);
assert(clean_email('') === null);

echo "ALL SANITIZATION TESTS PASSED\n";
```

### S010 — CSRF Protection
**One thing:** CSRF tokens generate, store, and validate correctly. Replay attacks blocked.
**Why its own session:** CSRF is a cross-cutting security concern. One missed verification = account takeover. Test every edge case.

| Task | Status |
|------|--------|
| `generate_csrf_token()` — 64-char hex, stored in session | ✅ |
| `verify_csrf_token(token)` — constant-time comparison | ✅ |
| `verify_csrf_token()` returns false for wrong token | ✅ |
| `verify_csrf_token()` returns false for empty/null | ✅ |
| `verify_csrf_token()` returns false if no session | ✅ |
| API bootstrap: POST requests verify CSRF header | ✅ |
| HTML forms: hidden CSRF field auto-included in header.php | ✅ |
| `API.post()` in app.js: auto-sends CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token header | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```php
session_start();

$token = generate_csrf_token();
assert(strlen($token) === 64, 'token must be 64 chars');
assert(ctype_xdigit($token), 'token must be hex');

// Valid token
assert(verify_csrf_token($token) === true, 'valid token must pass');

// Wrong token
assert(verify_csrf_token('wrongtoken') === false, 'wrong token must fail');
assert(verify_csrf_token('') === false, 'empty token must fail');
assert(verify_csrf_token(null) === false, 'null token must fail');

// Timing attack: verify uses hash_equals not ==
// (inspect code — must use hash_equals)

// Each call generates NEW token (tokens don't reuse)
$token2 = generate_csrf_token();
assert($token !== $token2, 'each call must generate unique token');

echo "ALL CSRF TESTS PASSED\n";
```

### S011 — Permission System: can() + require_permission()

| `current_user()` — returns session array or null | ✅ |
| `require_permission(module, action)` — calls http_response_code(403) + exit | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```php
// Mock session for testing
$_SESSION['ff_user'] = [
    'id' => 1,
    'role_slug' => 'accountant',
    'permissions' => [
        'invoices' => ['view'=>1,'create'=>1,'edit'=>1,'delete'=>0,'export'=>1],
        'customers' => ['view'=>1,'create'=>0,'edit'=>0,'delete'=>0,'export'=>0],
        'users'     => ['view'=>0,'create'=>0,'edit'=>0,'delete'=>0,'export'=>0],
    ]
];

// Accountant can view + create invoices
assert(can('invoices', 'view') === true);
assert(can('invoices', 'create') === true);

// Accountant cannot delete invoices or manage users
assert(can('invoices', 'delete') === false);
assert(can('users', 'view') === false);
assert(can('customers', 'create') === false);

// Super admin can do anything
$_SESSION['ff_user']['role_slug'] = 'super_admin';
assert(can('users', 'delete') === true);
assert(can('nonexistent_module', 'view') === true);

// No session
unset($_SESSION['ff_user']);
assert(can('invoices', 'view') === false);
assert(current_user() === null);
assert(is_super_admin() === false);

echo "ALL PERMISSION TESTS PASSED\n";
```

### S013 — Login Page + Brute Force Protection
**One thing:** Login form works. Brute force is blocked. No username enumeration.
**Contract: POST /auth/login.php**
```
Request: { email, password, csrf_token, remember_me? }
Success: redirect to dashboard (or redirect_after_login)
Failures:
  missing CSRF              → 403
  invalid credentials       → 200 with error (never specify which field)
  account locked            → 200 with locked message + unlock time
  account inactive/invited  → 200 with appropriate message
```

| Task | Status |
|------|--------|
| `app/auth/login.php` — form page + POST handler | ✅ |
| CSRF token verified on POST | ✅ |
| email + password from POST via clean_email() + clean_string() | ✅ |
| `password_verify()` with bcrypt | ✅ |
| login_attempts counter incremented on failure | ✅ |
| After 5 failures in 60 min → `locked_until` set to +15 min | ✅ |
| Locked account check runs BEFORE password check | ✅ |
| Generic error message always (never "wrong email" vs "wrong password") | ✅ |
| Successful login: session_regenerate_id(true) | ✅ |
| Successful login: $_SESSION['ff_user'] populated with permissions | ✅ |
| Successful login: audit_log entry (action=login) | ✅ |
| Failed login: audit_log entry (action=login, notes=failed) | ✅ |
| "Remember me": separate 30-day secure cookie | ✅ |

**Stop conditions:**
```
HAPPY PATH:
  POST valid email + password → session created → redirect to dashboard

ENUMERATION CHECK (critical):
  POST valid email + wrong password → "Invalid email or password"
  POST invalid email + anything → EXACT same message, same timing
  (timing attack: both paths must take same time — no early exit on email check)

BRUTE FORCE:
  POST wrong credentials 4× → still "Invalid email or password"
  POST wrong credentials 5× → "Account locked for 15 minutes"
  POST correct credentials while locked → still "locked" (lock checked first)
  Wait 15 min (mock locked_until to past) → login works again

CSRF:
  POST without CSRF token → 403
  POST with wrong CSRF token → 403

AUDIT LOG:
  Successful login: audit_log has action=login, user_id set, ip_address set
  Failed login: audit_log has action=login, notes contains "failed attempt N"
  Locked: audit_log has action=login, notes contains "account locked"

SESSION SECURITY:
  Session ID BEFORE login !== session ID AFTER login (regenerated)
  Session cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
```

**INSPECTION FORM DESIGN (based on physical inspection sheet — 2026-04-03):**

The physical form has two identical panels side-by-side (one for PRE-lease OUT, one for POST-lease IN). Each panel contains:

**Panel: Header fields**

**Bugs found and fixed during stop-condition testing:**
- `db_sanitize_column()` did not backtick-quote column names — `condition` (MySQL reserved word) caused SQLSTATE[42000] syntax error on `db_insert('inspection_sections', ...)`. Fixed: `db_sanitize_column()` now returns `` `{$col}` `` (backtick-wrapped).
- `api/v1/inspections/show.php` and `app/admin/inspections/show.php` both referenced `et.unit_type` — column is actually `et.category`. Fixed: aliased as `et.category AS unit_type` in both queries.

## GLOBAL STANDARDS

| Standard | Rule |
|----------|------|
| **Soft deletes** | Every query on the 15 SOFT_DELETE_TABLES includes `AND {table}.deleted_at IS NULL` |
| **SOFT_DELETE_TABLES** | users, customers, customer_notes, equipment_templates, equipment_units, leases, damage_claims, invoices, maintenance_work_orders, documents, vendors, credit_notes, reservations, rate_cards, payments [PASS-13:F2] |
| **DB helpers only** | NEVER raw `$pdo->query()` — always the typed helpers |
| **Output escaping** | NEVER raw echo of any user/DB data — always `e()` |
| **Input cleaning** | All POST/GET data through clean_*() before use |
| **Monetary** | DECIMAL(12,2) in DB — NEVER float. bcmath in PHP — NEVER float operators [PASS-10:6] |
| **UTC** | Store UTC, display via format_datetime() in company timezone |
| **Strict types** | `<?php declare(strict_types=1);` — first line of every PHP file |
| **API format** | `{success:true,data:{},meta:{}}` or `{success:false,error_code:"",message:""}` |
| **Numbers are links** | Every count/KPI/summary value drills down |
| **DM Mono** | All numbers, amounts, dates, codes use DM Mono |
| **State machines** | Invalid transitions → 409. All transitions → status_log. |
| **File uploads** | finfo_file() MIME check, safe rename, ALL uploads via StorageClient [INFRA] — NEVER move_uploaded_file() directly |
| **Row locking** | Lease creation, lease close, payment allocation, credit application — all use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside db_transaction() [PASS-8:4, D20] |
| **Optimistic locking** | All update endpoints compare updated_at before saving → 409 STALE_DATA if stale [PASS-8:4G, D19] |
| **Cron locks** | Every write-heavy cron uses MySQL GET_LOCK() advisory lock to prevent duplicate runs [D21] |
| **Audit logging** | Every write: user_id, action, module, entity_type, entity_id, old_values, new_values |
| **Permission gates** | PHP enforces. JS only hides for UX. Both always present. |
| **Validation** | Server-side always. Client-side for UX only — never trusted. |
| **Business logic** | Lives in PHP only. Never in JS. Never split across both. |
| **Denormalized counters** | Updated in the SAME transaction as the triggering event |
| **Portal isolation** | Every portal query: AND customer_id = portal_customer_id() |
| **Billing math** | Pure classes: no DB, bcmath only [PASS-10:6]. InvoiceGenerator: only class that writes. Day count: inclusive (end-start+1) [PASS-3:1A]. |
| **Contract first** | Every API session starts with written contract, approved before code |

## Footnote — 2026-04-07 · VALID-2 Form Validation Messages (continuation session)

**What was just done in this session:**

1. **Verified 15 accounting admin pages already wire `.field-error` slots + `.form-error-banner` banners** against per-form `errors{}` state and clear-on-input handlers (statements, bank-accounts, journal-entries, bank-reconciliation, depreciation, capex, fixed-assets, tax, settings, bills, vendor-credits, deposits, collections, categorization-rules, chart-of-accounts). All use the shared helper triplet `_extractError / _clearErrors / _paintErrors` and `:class="errors.X ? 'is-invalid' : ''"` bindings. ~400 error markers total.

2. **Fixed 2 real server-side VALID-2 violations** discovered by the new smoke test:
   - `api/v1/vendors/create.php` — was fail-fast `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …, 422)` on first bad field. Refactored to accumulate every guard (name / vendor_type / email / rating / hourly_rate / specializations) into `$fields[]` and emit **one** `json_validation_error()` call. Duplicate-name collisions now also flow through the standard `fields` envelope so the client can highlight the offending input.
   - `api/v1/yards/create.php` — was emitting a bespoke `['errors' => [...]]` extra key and failing fast on missing name. Refactored to use the standard `fields` envelope, accumulate name + capacity + manager_id guards, and route duplicate-name collisions through `json_validation_error()`.

3. **New smoke-test harness — `tests/_smoke_valid2.php`** (~310 lines):
   - Manually writes a real PHP session file to `/var/tmp/sess_<id>` (the path Herd PHP-FPM reads from — **not** CLI PHP's `/var/folders/.../T/`), injecting a super_admin `ff_user` payload + `csrf_token` so we can authenticate cURL calls against the live Herd endpoints without going through the interactive login flow.
   - POSTs 30 bad payloads and asserts each response is `HTTP 422` + `success=false` + `error.code='VALIDATION_ERROR'` + `error.fields` containing the expected field keys.
   - Coverage: Journal Entry (empty / 1-line / unbalanced), Bank Account, Bank Transfer, Bill, Tax Period (bad type / end-before-start), CapEx, Vendor Credit, AR Deposit, Customer (empty / bad email / discount > 100 / negative credit), Equipment Unit (empty / bad year), Lease, Invoice (empty / bad period), Payment (empty / negative amount), Vendor, Reservation, Damage Claim, Maintenance WO, Inspection, Mileage Log, Yard.
   - `register_shutdown_function` unlinks the session file on exit; defensive cleanup deletes any stray `Smoke Acme%` customer rows at the end of the run so the test is idempotent.

**Final smoke-test result: `PASS: 30    FAIL: 0    SKIP: 0    TOTAL: 30`**

**Standards reinforced:**
- `json_validation_error(array $fields, ?string $message = null)` in `api/bootstrap.php` is the **only** form-validation response helper. No more fail-fast `json_error('MISSING_REQUIRED', …)` on first bad field. No more bespoke `['errors' => [...]]` extra keys.
- Every create/update endpoint must accumulate errors into `$fields[]` and emit exactly one `json_validation_error($fields)` call before any insert.
- Client forms must paint errors into inline `.field-error` slots + a top `.form-error-banner`, clear on `@input` / `@change`, and short-circuit submit on client-side `validate*()` helpers.

Root cause: the modal outer wrapper used `class="modal-backdrop"` — the CSS class that provides the dark blurred backdrop (`position:fixed; inset:0; background:rgba(0,0,0,0.70); backdrop-filter:blur(4px); z-index:0`) but has **no** `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center`. Those centering properties live on `.modal-overlay`. So `.modal.modal-sm` was a block child of a fixed div with no flex centering, which positioned it at the top-left corner. Also found a secondary bug: the modal close button used `class="modal-close"` but the design system CSS only defines `.modal-close-btn`. **Fix in `app/admin/compliance/index.php`:** Changed outer `<div class="modal-backdrop" x-show="modal.open" x-cloak>` to `<div class="modal-overlay" x-show="modal.open" x-cloak @click.self="closeModal()" style="background:rgba(0,0,0,0.70);backdrop-filter:blur(4px);-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(4px);">` — using `modal-overlay` for fixed-position flex centering while preserving the dark backdrop via inline style. Changed close button from `class="modal-close"` → `class="modal-close-btn"`. PHP syntax verified clean. No other files modified. Previous: SIDEBAR-SCROLL-1 Sidebar Scroll Fix complete:* On short-viewport laptops / tablets / mobile, the left sidebar was not scrolling — bottom nav items (Settings, Users, Vendors, etc.) were cut off at the viewport bottom and unreachable. Root cause was three interacting bugs in `public/assets/css/app.css`: (1) base `.sidebar` rule had `overflow-y: auto` on the outer `<aside>` element, which meant the whole sidebar scrolled as a unit — pushing the brand header off the top and the user footer off the bottom as the user scrolled; (2) the inner `.sidebar-nav` had `flex: 1` without `min-height: 0`, the classic flexbox-child scroll gotcha where `flex: 1` refuses to shrink below content height, so even if you added `overflow: auto` to the nav it would never actually scroll; (3) the tablet media query (`@media (min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1023px)`) had an explicit `overflow: visible` override which killed every form of scroll containment on the icon rail, leaving overflow items to spill invisibly off the bottom of the viewport. **Fix — `public/assets/css/app.css`:** base `.sidebar` changed from `overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: hidden; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.1) transparent` to `overflow: hidden` (outer now clips, does not scroll) with a comment explaining why brand + footer stay pinned. `.sidebar-nav` rewritten from `flex: 1; padding: 12px 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px` to add `flex: 1 1 0; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; overflow-x: hidden; scroll-behavior: smooth; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: transparent transparent` plus a `:hover` rule that swaps the thumb to `rgba(255,255,255,0.18)` for a clean "reveal on hover" effect, matched by four `::-webkit-scrollbar*` rules for Blink/WebKit (`width: 4px`, transparent track, transparent thumb → opaque on hover, 0.2s ease transition). Tablet rule at line 4964 `.sidebar { ... overflow: visible }` changed to `overflow: hidden` with a comment about why `visible` broke inner scroll. **Fix — `includes/sidebar.php`:** appended an inline `<script>` block after `</aside>` that scrolls the active nav item into view on page load. Initial attempt used `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: 'auto' })` per the spec but Chrome silently no-op'd on the real layout — verified via `preview_eval`: `beforeScroll=0, afterScroll=0, activeMoved=false` even though the active Settings item was positioned at `top: 468, bottom: 484` entirely below a nav viewport ending at `y=433`. Switched to a manual scroll-math approach: bail early if `active` is already fully inside the nav's scroll viewport (no unnecessary scroll); otherwise compute `targetTop = active.offsetTop - (nav.clientHeight/2) + (active.offsetHeight/2)`, clamp to `[0, scrollHeight - clientHeight]`, and set `scrollTop` with `scroll-behavior: auto` to avoid a visible jump on initial paint while Alpine is still mounting sidebar group state. Guards against missing nav/active element. Runs once on `DOMContentLoaded` (or immediately if DOM is already past loading). **Verification via preview_eval on the live Herd server** (logged in as Carol/manager3, the pure-manager user with the longest sidebar): **(1) 1280×600 desktop-short** — `sidebar.overflow: hidden, canScroll: false; sidebarNav.flex: 1 1 0px, minHeight: 0px, overflowY: auto, scrollBehavior: smooth, scrollbarWidth: thin, scrollHeight: 513 > clientHeight: 473, canScroll: true`; brand flex-shrink 0, height 60; footer flex-shrink 0, height 67. **(2) 1280×500 tightest-laptop** — after manually scrolling `.sidebar-nav` to `scrollTop: 139.5 / maxScroll: 140`, Settings (`/fleetforge/settings`) at `top: 347, bottom: 363` sits inside the nav slot (`60–433`), `visibleInNav: true, visibleInViewport: true`. Brand `top: 0, bottom: 60`, footer `top: 433, bottom: 500` — both pinned. **(3) 900×600 tablet** after hard reload — `sidebar.position: fixed, width: 64px` (icon rail), `overflowY: hidden`; nav `overflowY: auto, scrollHeight: 609 > clientHeight: 439, canScroll: true, scrollTopAfterJump: 170 === maxScroll: 170`. **(4) 441×824 mobile overlay** with `is-open` forced — sidebar `position: fixed, transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` (translated into view), `overflowY: hidden`; nav `scrollHeight: 1162 > clientHeight: 696`, max-scroll 466; after jump-to-bottom `scrollTopAfter: 466.5`, Settings at `top: 636, bottom: 680` is `visibleInViewport: true && visibleInNavSlot: true`; brand and footer pinned (`top: 0, bottom: 60` and `top: 755.5, bottom: 824.5`). **(5) Active-item scrollIntoView verification** — navigated to `/fleetforge/settings` at 1280×500 with Carol, hard-reloaded, inspected `.sidebar-nav` immediately after page load: `navScrollTop: 121.5, navMaxScroll: 122` (JS auto-scrolled the nav on initial paint), Settings at `top: 347, bottom: 363` inside nav box `top: 60, bottom: 433`, `visibleInNav: true`. **(6) Full desktop 1440×900 no-op check** — on a tall viewport, `navScrollHeight: 773 === navClientHeight: 773, canScroll: false, noScrollNeeded: true, navScrollTop: 0` (early-bail path in the JS fires, no unwanted scroll). **(7) Smooth scroll bug debug** — early test showed `nav.scrollTop = N` reading back as `0`; confirmed not a bug but a race with `scroll-behavior: smooth` which animates the assignment asynchronously — forcing `nav.style.scrollBehavior = 'auto'` during the test read-back returned the expected value, proving the scroll itself was functional. **(8) Scrolling-ancestor inspection** — walked up from active nav item, confirmed `NAV.sidebar-nav` is the single scrolling ancestor (`overflowY: auto, scrollHeight: 495 > clientHeight: 373, canScroll: true`), so `scrollIntoView` couldn't have accidentally scrolled a different ancestor. **Checklist, all PASS:** ☑ browser at 768px height — all sidebar items accessible by scrolling; ☑ scrollbar hidden until `.sidebar-nav:hover`; ☑ brand stays fixed at top while nav scrolls; ☑ active item centered in nav on page load when offscreen; ☑ tablet icon rail (64px, 768-1023px) scrolls; ☑ mobile overlay (<768px) scrolls when is-open; ☑ scrolling the sidebar does NOT scroll main content (scrollingAncestors=1, only `.sidebar-nav`); ☑ main content scrolls independently (sidebar is `position: sticky` on desktop, `position: fixed` on tablet/mobile); ☑ bottom nav items (Settings, Users) reachable; ☑ no layout shift when sidebar scrolls (brand/footer have `flex-shrink: 0` and fixed heights). **Noted (not failures)**: 441×824 "mobile" viewport the preview harness reported is above the 375×700 I requested — Chrome emulation scale quirk — the actual media query evaluated against `innerWidth = 441` which is still <768, so mobile overlay rules apply. Tablet `is-open` state showed width 240px (stuck expanded) until hard reload, because Alpine `sidebarOpen` state persisted from desktop; after reload it correctly rendered the 64px rail. These are pre-existing Alpine state quirks unrelated to SIDEBAR-SCROLL-1. **Regression caught + fixed (same session):** after the initial CSS landed, the user reported "everything's squished" on full-screen desktop. Root cause was that `min-height: 0` on `.sidebar-nav` (required for the `overflow: auto` to fire) allowed its direct children — which are themselves flex items because `.sidebar-nav` is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` — to shrink below their natural height via the default `flex-shrink: 1`. Nav items that should have been 39px each were compressing to ~24px, crushing the sidebar visually. Fixed by adding a `.sidebar-nav > * { flex-shrink: 0 }` rule right after the `.sidebar-nav` block. Verified at 1440×900: all 25 direct children report `flex-shrink: 0` and `offsetHeight: 39` (not 24), the nav still scrolls correctly (`scrollHeight: 1037 > clientHeight: 773, canScroll: true`) on Carol's full manager sidebar. Verified at 1280×500 /settings: first 5 items all 39px (not squished), auto-scroll still centers Settings at `top: 306, bottom: 345` inside nav, `visibleInNav: true`. Screenshot confirms natural spacing restored. **Files modified in this session:** `public/assets/css/app.css` (3 edits: base `.sidebar` block → `overflow: hidden`; `.sidebar-nav` rewrite with min-height/overflow/scroll-behavior/scrollbar rules + 5 `::-webkit-scrollbar*` rules + hover reveal + the `.sidebar-nav > * { flex-shrink: 0 }` regression fix; 1 edit: tablet media query `overflow: visible` → `overflow: hidden`), `includes/sidebar.php` (inline `<script>` appended after `</aside>` with manual scroll-math scrollIntoView), `FLEETFORGE_PROGRESS.md` (this footnote). No build step — CSS is served directly, no cache-busting version bump needed since nginx serves `?v=1.0.15` but Herd has disk-level auto-reload.
